  "abstract_verbatim": "For every <i>n</i> ≥ 1 and prime $`p\\gt n+1`$, we construct a $`2^n`$-stage ordered filtration of $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\\wedge`$ with the classical chromatic-splitting cofibers. The map from the first stage to the target is the canonical localization unit.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every <i>n</i> ≥ 1 and prime $`p\gt n+1`$, we construct a $`2^n`$-stage ordered filtration of $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge`$ with the classical chromatic-splitting cofibers. The map from the first stage to the target is the canonical localization unit.

- **claim-ordered-filtration** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): Let $n\geq1$ and let $p>n+1$ be prime. There exist an enumeration $I_1,\ldots,I_{2^n}$ of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a filtration $F_\bullet$, and a family of classes $y_i\in\pi_{1-2i}D$, $1\leq i\leq n$, with the following properties.* 1. ***Filtration and unit.** The enumeration has $I_1=\varnothing$ and $\max I_j$ nondecreasing for $j\geq2$. The filtration is $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots \longrightarrow F_{2^n}\xrightarrow{\simeq}X_{n,p}$$ with $\operatorname{cofib}(F_{j-1}\to F_j)\simeq C_{I_j}$, where $$\label{eq:pieces} \begin{aligned} C_\varnothing&=L_{n-1}S,\\ C_I&=\Sigma^{-d(I)}L_{n-\max I}S \quad(I\ne\varnothing). \end{aligned}$$ Under $F_1=C_\varnothing$, the composite $F_1\to X_{n,p}$ is the canonical localization unit.* 2. ***Simultaneous product bases.** For this one family, set $y_\varnothing=1$ and $y_I=y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_r}$ for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_r\}$. For every $1\leq t<n$, the specified map $$\label{eq:height-basis} L_{K(t)} \left(\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}} \Sigma^{-d(I)}S\xrightarrow{(y_I)}D\right) \quad\text{is an equivalence}.$$
  - Explanation: Constructs an ordered chromatic filtration with its canonical unit and a common family of product bases, retaining attaching maps.
- **claim-filtration-criterion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-assembly)): Let $n\geq1$, let $p$ be odd, and let $D$ be an $S$-module with a specified map $u:S\to D$. Suppose that maps $$z_I:\Sigma^{-d(I)}S\longrightarrow D, \qquad I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}, \qquad z_\varnothing=u,$$ have the following properties.* 1. *For each $1\leq t<n$, the map with the specified components $$\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}}\Sigma^{-d(I)}S \xrightarrow{(z_I)} D \label{eq:criterion-bases}$$ is a $K(t)$-equivalence.* 2. *For every integer $b$, $$\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}L_0D =\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\}. \label{eq:criterion-rational}$$ If $n=1$, assume in addition that $\pi_0L_0u$ is nonzero.* *Then $X=L_{n-1}D$ has the filtration and unit compatibility of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>(a), with $u$ in place of its unit.
  - Explanation: Compatible specified local bases and rational dimensions assemble into a filtration whose first map is the prescribed unit.
- **claim-finite-labeled-rings** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-finite-rings)): There are compatible identifications $$\label{rings:regular-coordinates} C_l=k[[w_{1,l},\ldots,w_{m,l}]],\qquad \widetilde C_l=k[[z_{1,l},\ldots,z_{m,l}]],\qquad w_{i,l}=z_{i,l}^{p^{tl}}.$$ Both rings are finite free over $A$. On the exact-height locus, $C_l[1/x]$ is the finite étale algebra of bases of the étale $p^l$-torsion. Over this algebra the scheme of all lifts of its universal basis to $\mathcal G_A[p^l]$ has algebra $$\widetilde C_l[1/x]=(C_l[1/x])^{1/p^{tl}},$$ finite locally free of rank $p^{tlm}$.* *The transition maps are finite and injective, and for $j\leq l$ $$\label{rings:transition-powers} z_{i,j}\in k[[z_{1,l}^{p^{t(l-j)}},\ldots,z_{m,l}^{p^{t(l-j)}}]].$$
  - Explanation: Identifies labeled and lifted torsion rings as regular power-series rings, including the unreduced finite lift scheme and its transitions.
- **claim-integral-full-sections** (classification, [source](#stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation)): Let $H$ be the quotient of $\mathcal G_A[p]$ by its relative $p^t$-Frobenius kernel. The ring $C_1$ represents full labeled section tuples $\mathbb F_p^m\to H$, including over nilpotent test rings. Here “full” means equality of the finite Cartier divisors, or equivalently, after every base change, equality of the norm of every function with its product over the labeled sections.
  - Explanation: The labeled ring represents full section tuples over arbitrary test rings, retaining nilpotent information through the norm condition.
- **claim-boundary-labels** (classification, [source](#stmt-rings-boundary-labels)): At level one, for each nonzero label $v\in\mathbb F_p^m$ there is a coordinate $w_v$ such that $$\label{rings:height-divisor} x=\text{a unit}\cdot\prod_{0\ne v\in\mathbb F_p^m}w_v.$$ Each ideal $(w_v)$ is $P_n$-stable. Its conormal is a power of the invariant coordinate line. For a primitive label, the quotient by $(w_v)$ is the starting-height-$(t+1)$ level-one ring with $p$-th roots of its parameters adjoined. The same assertion can be iterated for any independent set of dead labels.
  - Explanation: Label divisors factor the height parameter and identify successive dead-label boundaries with rooted higher-starting-height discs.
- **claim-frame-lift-torsors** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-frame-torsor)): The rings $B_U$ form a tower of finite étale $B$-algebras. After passing to normal open levels, the maps in the tower are finite étale torsors for the indicated finite deck groups. The tower is $P_n$-equivariant, and $P_n$ commutes with its $U_0$-action.* *Over $\mathcal B$, the scheme of lifts of the compatible étale basis is an affine faithfully flat torsor for $$\label{rings:translation-group} T=(T_p\Gamma_t)^m, \qquad T_p\Gamma_t=\varprojlim_{[p]}\Gamma_t[p^r].$$ For every $r\geq1$ its finite quotient has group $T/[p]^rT=\Gamma_t[p^r]^m$ and algebra $$\label{rings:root-torsor} \mathcal B^{1/p^{tr}}.$$ Thus the full lift algebra is the algebraic root union $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{perf}}$. The group $P_n$ acts trivially on the translation parameters. The action of $(h,a)\in U_0$ on a translation tuple $\tau$ is $$\label{rings:auxiliary-action} \tau\longmapsto h\tau a^{-1}.$$ All finite torsor constructions and all their morphisms descend to finite frame levels once their finite marking data are included.
  - Explanation: Constructs commuting frame actions and faithfully flat translation torsors whose finite lift algebras are root extensions.
- **claim-divisible-frobenius-levels** (construction, [source](#stmt-rings-dual-distribution)): There is a positive integer $r_0$, divisible by $t-1$, such that for $r=ar_0$, $a\geq1$, the two numbers $$\label{rings:two-frobenius-indices} Q=p^{tr},\qquad q=p^{tr/(t-1)}$$ are Frobenius powers fixing $k$. At this level $$\mathcal O((\Gamma_t^\vee[p^r])^m) =\Lambda_q:=\Lambda/(D_1^q,\ldots,D_d^q), \qquad \dim_k\Lambda_q=q^d=Q^m.$$ The embedding $[p]^r:T\hookrightarrow T$ corresponds on distributions to $$\psi_q:\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda, \qquad D_j\longmapsto D_j^q,\quad c\longmapsto c\ (c\in k).$$ If $N_q=\mathcal O(T/[p]^rT)$ is the regular function representation, finite Hopf duality gives a normalized equivariant identification $N_q\simeq\Lambda_q$ as translation representations. The auxiliary action on each finite quotient factors through a finite group.
  - Explanation: Chooses divisible levels distinguishing function-root and distribution exponents and identifies regular translation representations equivariantly.
- **claim-powering-associated-diagrams** (construction, [source](#stmt-rings-coinduction)): Let $r$ be one of the chosen levels and put $H=[p]^rT$. Transport a finite $T$-representation $M$ to $H$ using $[p]^r:T\simeq H$, and then coinduce it to $T$. This is an exact functor, denoted $\mathcal C_r$. There is a natural $P_n$- and auxiliary-equivariant identification of the associated coefficient diagram for $\mathcal C_rM$ with the $Q$-root version of the diagram for $M$. Powering by $Q$ identifies the two diagrams $k$-linearly and Frobenius-semilinearly over the base: $$\label{rings:power-scalar-rule} \Phi_Q(cf)=c^Q\Phi_Q(f),\qquad \Phi_Q(f)=f^Q.$$ The assertion holds for every morphism and every finite diagram, and after invariants in any compatible open frame subgroup. It does not require trivializing the auxiliary action on all coinduced modules simultaneously.
  - Explanation: Coinduction transports entire associated coefficient diagrams to root diagrams, with actual equivariant Frobenius powering.
- **claim-cartier-transfer-transpose** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-cartier-transfer)): Fix one sufficiently divisible step with function-root exponent $Q$, and use the volume just constructed. The quotient transfers of the lift torsors can be normalized compatibly so that, after powering to a fixed finite frame ring, their first step is $$\label{rings:stationary-c} S(f)=\frac{\mathscr C_Q(f\eta)}{\eta},$$ where $\mathscr C_Q$ is Cartier trace on continuous top differentials. The subsequent stationary transfers are $S^a$. In particular $S(c^Qf)=cS(f)$.* *These transfers are finite Hopf integration on the torsor, not ordinary field trace. They commute with $P_n$, with their natural auxiliary actions, and with finite étale change of frame level. Their transpose under the residue pairing is positive Frobenius on dual coefficient functions, with the one volume line <a href="#rings:volume-character" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:volume-character">[rings:volume-character]</a> retained. Before stationary identification it is the inclusion into the next root coefficient ring. For a finite étale cover or its associated coefficient module, this is the actual Frobenius on the cover functions and their trace duals. All statements hold for finite diagrams in Lemma <a href="#rings:coinduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rings:coinduction">10</a>.
  - Explanation: Normalizes torsor integration so its stationary form is Cartier transfer and its residue transpose is actual positive Frobenius with the volume line retained.
- **claim-coefficient-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-coefficient-finiteness)): Suppose $1\leq t<n<p-1$. The following assertions hold.* 1. *Every admissible compact coefficient on $A$ or $C_1$ has finite total continuous $P_n$-cohomology. This includes the stable finite free lattices constructed below.* 2. *For every finite joint frame level $U$, the bounded-pole groups $H^*(P_n,B_U)$ have finite total dimension. The assertion also holds with a fixed power of the invariant line. Finite direct sums and finite-dimensional trivial coefficient factors are allowed.* 3. *For every fixed compact open $V\subset\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_m(\mathbb Z_p)$, $H^*(P_n,B_{\mathrm{conn},V})$ has finite total dimension. There is an integer $h$, independent of the rectangular levels used in the union, such that $1+p^h\mathbb Z_p$ acting by scalar matrices acts identically on $H^*(P_n,B_{\mathrm{full}})$. These conclusions persist after taking the algebraic union of Frobenius roots, with the actions transported by powering.* *Moreover, put $B_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{perf}} =\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_r B_{\mathrm{full}}^{1/p^r}$, the algebraic root union with common finite stages on compact cochain sources. For every compact open $V\subset\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_m(\mathbb Z_p)$ and every $a,i$, the finite-dimensional smooth $P_t$-representation $$Q_{V}^{a,i}= H^a\!\left(V,H^i(P_n,B_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{perf}})\right)$$ has a finite $P_t$-stable filtration whose successive quotients are powers of the reduced-norm character $\nu_t$.* *All assertions use common finite stages on profinite cochain sources.
  - Explanation: Establishes compact, bounded-pole, and full-frame finiteness with uniform scalar triviality and norm-character filtrations on perfected individual rows.
- **claim-universal-norm-line** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-norm-line)): Let $\mathcal G$ be the algebraic height-$s$, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group obtained from the universal formal deformation, and let $\mathcal R_s$ be its characteristic-$p$ complete local deformation ring. There is a functorial height-one, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group $$\mathcal H_{\det}=\bigwedge^s\mathcal G.$$ Its marked deformation is canonically constant. The covariant action of $P_s$ on its special group, and hence on this constant marked deformation, is multiplication by the actual unit $\operatorname{Nrd}(g)\in\mathbb Z_p^\times$.* *With the convention that actions on functions use inverse substitution, put $$\mathcal N_s= \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal R_s}(\omega_{\mathcal H_{\det}},\mathcal R_s).$$ Then there is a $P_s$-equivariant identification $$\mathcal N_s\simeq \mathcal R_s\otimes_k k(\nu_s).$$ Every integral tensor power of this line is admissible on every starting-height quotient of the deformation disc and on its labeled disc. The assertion is preserved by the finite root transports and the successive boundary restrictions used in Definition <a href="#def:compact:admissible" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:compact:admissible">12</a>.
  - Explanation: Realizes the constant reduced-norm character through the determinant Barsotti–Tate group and proves admissibility across roots and boundaries.
- **claim-norm-filtered-coefficients** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-compact-norm-filtration)): Let $E$ be an admissible compact coefficient for a pair $(s,t)$, and let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth $P_s$-representation with a finite $P_s$-stable filtration $$0=Q_0\subset Q_1\subset\cdots\subset Q_l=Q, \qquad Q_j/Q_{j-1}\simeq k(\nu_s^{e_j}).$$ Then $E\otimes_k Q$ and $E\otimes_k Q^\vee$ are admissible. At every induction stage where compact finiteness at $(s,t)$ is available, their total $P_s$-cohomology is finite-dimensional.
  - Explanation: Tensoring admissible coefficients with norm-filtered representations or their duals preserves admissibility and available compact finiteness.
- **claim-transfer-stable-lattices** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-stable-lattices)): At a sufficiently deep finite joint frame level, the finite free coefficient $B_U$ and the associated coefficients of any fixed finite translation diagram admit $P_n$-stable free $C_1$-lattices. Their fixed pole strips have finite filtrations by boundary restrictions of admissible coefficients. For the stationary functions coefficient one can choose such a lattice $L$ and an integer $b$ so that $$P=x^{-b}L$$ is preserved by $S$, and every $x^{-c}L$ is carried into $P$ by a sufficiently high iterate of $S$. In the invariant-volume frames the transpose on the dual lattice of top forms has Frobenius matrix entries in $xC_1$. Its finite basis, viewed as finite-cover functions by these frames, can be taken integral over $C_1$.
  - Explanation: Builds stable free lattices, controls fixed pole strips, and arranges transfer stability together with integral positive Frobenius on the dual.
- **claim-compact-residue-duality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-duality)): Let $L$ be a stable finite free lattice over a formal $r$-disc $C$, and let $\mathfrak m_C$ be its closed-point ideal. Put $L^*=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_C(L,C)$ and $\omega_C=\bigwedge^r\widehat\Omega^1_{C/k}$, using continuous differentials. There are natural identifications $$\begin{aligned} L^\vee&\simeq H^r_{\mathfrak m_C}(L^*\otimes_C\omega_C),\\ H^i(P_n,L)^\vee &\simeq H^{n^2-i}\bigl(P_n,L^\vee\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ Here $(-)^\vee=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{k,\mathrm{cts}}(-,k)$ is the discrete continuous dual. The identifications are compatible with finite coefficient diagrams and with the transpose of the constant-cochain cup action. In particular $H^i(P_n,L)$ is profinite and vanishes outside $0\leq i\leq n^2$.
  - Explanation: Combines residue duality with orientable analytic group duality, preserving coefficient diagrams and transposed constant cup actions.
- **claim-perfected-honda-balls** (classification, [source](#stmt-support-tate-ball)): After scalar extension to $E$, the completed perfection of the full etale-basis tower, including its boundary, is the product of $m$ open Honda balls. The exact-height locus is the open locus on which the corresponding $m$ rational Tate sections are independent. The identification is compatible with $P_n$, changes of integral Tate basis, and passage between finite frame levels.
  - Explanation: Identifies the perfected full Tate-coordinate tower including its boundary with Honda balls and detects exact height by rational independence.
- **claim-geometric-frame-quotient** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-geometric-quotient)): Let $\mathcal X$ be the full perfected joint frame space over $E$. There is a $P_n\times U_0$-equivariant description of $\mathcal X$ as the space of exact sequences $$\label{support:framed-extension} 0\longrightarrow\mathcal O^m\longrightarrow V_n \longrightarrow V_t\longrightarrow0$$ whose determinant comparison is a $\mathbb Z_p^\times$-multiple of a fixed comparison. Forgetting the middle frame gives a $P_n$-torsor $\mathcal X\to Z$. Thus, for every compact open $U\subset U_0$, $$\label{support:quotient-stacks} [\mathcal X/U\,/P_n]\simeq[Z/U].$$ On the quotient there is the universal sequence $$0\longrightarrow L_m\otimes\mathcal O\longrightarrow V_n' \longrightarrow V_t'\longrightarrow0,$$ where $L_m$ has its integral etale lattice and the two positive bundles have compact frame reductions. Finally, $$\label{support:additive-presentation} N_t\simeq\mathbb A_C^{1,\diamond}/F,$$ where $F/\mathbb Q_p$ is unramified of degree $t$, acting by translations.
  - Explanation: Describes the frame space by determinant-matched bundle extensions and identifies its stabilizer quotient with the independent extension locus.
- **claim-solid-finite-resolution** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-solid-rows)): Let $K$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group without $p$-torsion, and put $R_K=\mathbb F_p[[K]]$. Let $\mathcal V$ be a solid $\mathbb F_p$-module with continuous condensed $K$-action. Choose a bounded resolution $Q_\bullet\to\mathbb F_p$ by finitely generated projective profinite $R_K$-modules. Then continuous solid $K$-cohomology is computed by $$\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{\underline{R_K}} (\underline{Q_\bullet},\mathcal V). \label{eq:const-solid-resolution}$$ Evaluation of this complex at the one-point profinite set is exact and each of its terms is a retract of a finite direct sum of $\mathcal V(*)$. In particular, if a commuting endomorphism $u$ acts as a scalar $c$ on $\mathcal V(*)$, it acts as $c$ on the point-valued cohomology of <a href="#eq:const-solid-resolution" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:const-solid-resolution">[eq:const-solid-resolution]</a>.* *For a derived solid coefficient $\mathcal A$, this gives a natural spectral sequence $$H^r_{\mathrm{solid}}(K;H^s(\mathcal A))(*) \ \Longrightarrow\ H^{r+s}(R\Gamma_{\mathrm{solid}}(K;\mathcal A))(*). \label{eq:const-solid-ss}$$ The preceding scalar assertion applies to every row.
  - Explanation: A finite projective profinite resolution computes solid group cohomology and preserves scalar actions under exact point evaluation and derived rows.
- **claim-compact-parameter-compatibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-support-parameters)): These localization and support computations are compatible with compact profinite parameters and compact frame torsors. They apply to the rational-rank loci in $N_t^m$ and to their flag incidences. On an exact-rank locus the smallest rational plane depends continuously on the point.
  - Explanation: Localization and support comparisons remain valid with compact parameters and torsors; smallest rational planes vary continuously on exact-rank strata.
- **claim-affine-diamond-supports** (classification, [source](#stmt-support-affine)): For the diamond of the untilted affine space one has $$R\Gamma_c(\mathbb A_C^{j,\diamond},\mathscr A) \simeq R(-j)[-2j].$$ Translations and invertible linear changes act trivially on this line, apart from its displayed arithmetic Tate twist. The identification is compatible with compact profinite parameters.
  - Explanation: Computes the compact-support line of untilted affine space, with arithmetic Tate twist and trivial affine-linear action.
- **claim-translation-quotient-supports** (classification, [source](#stmt-support-translation-quotient)): For $j\geq0$, $$\label{support:ambient-cohomology} R\Gamma_c(N_t^j,\mathscr A) \simeq R(-j)\otimes\operatorname{or}_{F^j}^{-1}[-(t+2)j].$$ Here $\operatorname{or}_{F^j}^{-1}$ is the top continuous cohomology orientation of a lattice in the $\mathbb Q_p$-space $F^j$. On $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_j(\mathbb Z_p)$ its character is $(\det)^{-t}$, reduced to the coefficient ring. The identification retains the commuting frame actions and compact parameters.
  - Explanation: Affine exhaustion and translation corestriction produce a single support line carrying the inverse lattice orientation.
- **claim-rational-flag-cohomology** (classification, [source](#stmt-support-flag-complex)): The complex <a href="#support:flag-complex-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="support:flag-complex-definition">[support:flag-complex-definition]</a> has cohomology only in degree $s$, where it is $\operatorname{St}(Q;M)$. The assertion is natural under linear isomorphisms and for locally constant families over compact rational Grassmannians.
  - Explanation: The augmented locally constant rational flag complex has only its top Steinberg cohomology, naturally in compact plane families.
- **claim-independent-locus-supports** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-compact-support)): The compactly supported cohomology of $Z$ is $$H_c^a(Z,\mathscr A)= \begin{cases} \mathcal V_j,&a=(t+2)j+(m-j),\quad 0\leq j<m,\\ \mathcal V_m,&a=(t+2)m,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$ The map to $R\Gamma_c(N_t^m,\mathscr A)$ identifies the last cohomology group with the ambient line. Scalar matrices in $1+p\mathbb Z_p$ act trivially on these cohomology groups. The statement is equivariant for the commuting compact frame groups and retains the actual finite incidence complex, without choosing an equivariant splitting of that complex.
  - Explanation: Computes support cohomology by plane dimension and retains the incidence complex, its frame actions, and the ambient top edge.
- **claim-support-invariants-finite** (bound, [source](#stmt-support-finite-invariants)): For a compact open $U\subset U_0$ and a fixed finite character twist, the groups $$H^a\bigl(U,R\Gamma_c(Z,\mathscr A)\otimes\chi\bigr)$$ vanish outside a finite range and have bounded almost length over $R$. In particular, if such a group is $V\otimes_kR$ for a $k$-vector space $V$, then $V$ is finite dimensional.
  - Explanation: Compact frame invariants of the twisted support complex have bounded almost length, detecting finite dimension before scalar extension.
- **claim-principal-parts-support-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-support-principal-parts)): On the perfected open $m$-disc, compact supports of the free integral lattice coefficient are computed by principal parts in degree $m$. For the root system of $M$, the resulting comparison is $$\label{support:principal-parts-comparison} \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{F} H^m_{\mathfrak m}(M)\otimes_kR[-m] \simeq R\Gamma_c\left(\mathbb D^{m,\mathrm{perf}}, \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_r\mathscr M_r\right),$$ where $\mathscr M_r$ and its transitions are defined above, and $F=S^\vee$ under <a href="#support:residue-dual" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="support:residue-dual">[support:residue-dual]</a>. The map is natural for lattice morphisms, integral coordinate changes, and continuous $P_n$ parameters.
  - Explanation: The positive root system on the perfected open disc is computed by a Frobenius colimit of algebraic principal parts with the residue shift.
- **claim-positive-extension-by-zero** (theorem, [source](#stmt-support-positive-extension)): There is a natural almost equivalence on the ambient perfected labelled disc $$\label{support:positive-extension-equivalence} \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_r\mathscr M_r \simeq j_!\nu_*\mathscr A_{\mathcal X/U} \otimes\langle\eta\rangle, \qquad j:\mathbb D^\times\hookrightarrow\mathbb D^{m,\mathrm{perf}}.$$ It respects finite-cover trace, changes of frame level, the $P_n$-action, and the retained volume character.
  - Explanation: The integral root-system colimit agrees almost with extension by zero from the finite punctured cover, retaining trace and volume actions.
- **claim-transpose-support-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-transpose-comparison)): For the stable lattice $P$ and sufficiently deep finite frame level $U$ specified above, there is a natural equivalence $$\label{support:transpose-derived} \left(\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{S^\vee} R\Gamma(P_n,P)^\vee\right)\otimes_kR \simeq R\Gamma\bigl(U,R\Gamma_c(Z,\mathscr A) \otimes\langle\eta\rangle\bigr)[m+n^2].$$ The dual of a compact cochain complex is its continuous $k$-linear dual, with cochain degrees reversed. In degree $-i$ this gives $$\label{support:transpose-cohomology} \left(\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{S^\vee}H^i(P_n,P)^\vee\right)\otimes_kR \simeq H^{m+n^2-i}\bigl(U,R\Gamma_c(Z,\mathscr A) \otimes\langle\eta\rangle\bigr).$$ These are equivalences of modules for the action of the actual constant $\mathbb F_p$-cochains of $P_n$, with the usual dual signs. Transpose trace upon enlargement of a frame level corresponds to pullback on the geometric side.
  - Explanation: Identifies dual transfer colimits with compact-support frame invariants as modules for the actual constant cochains, preserving trace directions.
- **claim-finite-stable-transfer-image** (bound, [source](#stmt-support-finite-stable-image)): For every $i$, the stable transfer image $$\bigcap_{r\geq0}S^rH^i(P_n,P)$$ is finite dimensional over $k$.
  - Explanation: The stable intersection of transfer images on compact lattice cohomology is finite dimensional.
- **claim-compact-operator-structure** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-operator)): Let $M$ be a compact $k$-vector space and $S$ a continuous $k$-linear endomorphism. Suppose $M/SM$ and $I=\bigcap_{a\geq0}S^aM$ are finite. Then $S(I)=I$, $S$ is invertible on $I$, and $M/I$ is a finitely generated $k[[z]]$-module with $z$ acting as $S$. In particular $S$ has finite kernel and cokernel on $M$.* *If $f:M\to X$ commutes with $S$ and has locally $S$-nilpotent kernel, then $\ker f$ is finite and $$\label{eq:compact:finite-intersection} \bigcap_{a\geq0}\operatorname{im}(S^aM\longrightarrow X)=f(I)$$ is finite.
  - Explanation: Finite cokernel and stable image control a compact operator through a finitely generated power-series module; locally nilpotent comparison kernels become finite.
- **claim-regular-system-pro-constant** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-pro-constant)): For each $i$, the pro object $\overline T^i(\Lambda)$ is constant and its augmentation to $T^i(k)$ is monic. Its $\Lambda$-action factors through $k$.
  - Explanation: The regular translation pro-system stabilizes modulo countable-dimensional spaces and injects into the trivial coefficient object.
- **claim-fixed-koszul-edge** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-koszul-edge)): For one sufficiently large allowed exponent $s$, a generator $e_s\in\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^d_\Lambda(N_s,k)$ induces an epimorphism $$T^{b_0-d}(N_s)\longrightarrow T^{b_0}(k)$$ in $\mathscr G$.
  - Explanation: A fixed sufficiently large Koszul extension surjects onto the highest potentially uncountable cohomology germ.
- **claim-uniform-equivariant-ext** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-uniform-ext)): Choose finite extension diagrams for $e_s$ as above and for a nonzero $e\in\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^d_\Lambda(k,k)$. They are equivariant for some compact open frame group $U$. For every allowed $q\geq s$ let $\gamma_q$ be the composite $$\label{eq:compact:coinduced-extension} N_s\longrightarrow N_q \xrightarrow{\operatorname{coind}(e)}N_q[d] \longrightarrow k[d],$$ where the outer maps are upward inclusion and normalized transfer. There is one open subgroup $U'\subset U$, independent of $q$, on which $$\gamma_q=c_qe_s, \qquad c_q\in k^\times,$$ as equivariant extensions.
  - Explanation: Fixed extension endpoints permit a common open frame subgroup on which all powered extension comparisons agree up to nonzero scalars.
- **claim-compact-coefficient-finiteness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-compact-finiteness)): The first assertion of Theorem <a href="#thm:coefficient-finiteness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:coefficient-finiteness">13</a> holds at $(n,t)$ under the earlier compact assertions in <a href="#eq:compact:induction-order" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact:induction-order">[eq:compact:induction-order]</a>. In addition, all finite-frame localized coefficients, and the localizations of admissible compact coefficients, have countable-dimensional $P_n$-cohomology.
  - Explanation: The inductive compact assertion follows by translation countability and compactness; localized coefficients are also shown countable dimensional.
- **claim-removal-of-pole-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-pole-removal)): Let $1\leq t<n<p-1$, and retain the notation $A$, $x=x_t$, and $C_1$ of Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-rings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-rings">4</a>. The bounded-pole continuous cohomology $$H^*(P_n,C_1[1/x]\otimes\omega^e),\qquad e\in\mathbb Z,$$ has finite total dimension over $k$, where $\omega$ is the invariant cotangent line of the universal connected formal group. Consequently $H^*(P_n,B_U)$ has finite total dimension at every finite joint frame level $U$; in particular this holds for every $B_{K,V}$.
  - Explanation: Boundary support descent upgrades localized coefficient countability to finite total cohomology, including invariant-line twists and finite frame levels.
- **claim-relative-artin-splitting** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-artin-splitting)): Set $R_N=R'/\mathfrak m'^{N}$. The marked height-$s$ nilpotent neighborhoods above are flat over $R_N$. After adjoining compatible lifts of the surviving étale basis, let $E_N$ be their algebraic union, formed first without the extra coefficient $C_1$. Then $$E_N/\mathfrak m'E_N=B_{\mathrm{full},s}^{\mathrm{perf}}=:S_s$$ is perfect, and there is a canonical isomorphism $$\label{eq:boundary-artin-product} R_N\otimes_k S_s \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } E_N.$$ It is compatible with restriction in $N$, with $P_n$, $P_s$, and the surviving matrix-group action, and with bounded-pole continuous cochains on every compact profinite source. The group translating the lifts remains the group over $R'$ determined by $\mathcal G$.
  - Explanation: Flat nilpotent marked neighborhoods split canonically into the Artin parameter algebra and their perfect special fiber, compatibly with bounded-pole cochains.
- **claim-full-sections-split-kernel** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-full-sections)): After the lift ascent of Lemma <a href="#lem:artin-splitting" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:artin-splitting">37</a>, the pullback of $C_1$ is a finite disjoint union of coefficients pulled back from $R'$ of the form $$\label{eq:boundary-M} M=C_1^{(s,t)}\otimes_{R'} \mathcal O(H_c)^{\otimes e_s}.$$ An invariant-line twist is the corresponding twist from $\mathcal G$. The algebra $M$ is finite free over $R'$, and is free over $C_1^{(s,t)}$ with finite torsion-coordinate factors. The decomposition and its group actions hold on arbitrary nilpotent test rings. A sufficiently small surviving matrix congruence subgroup fixes the components and acts trivially on the factors in <a href="#eq:boundary-M" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:boundary-M">[eq:boundary-M]</a>. Translation on these factors uses only a finite torsion level.
  - Explanation: The full-section coefficient decomposes across nilpotents into smaller-height labeled coefficients and finite connected torsion-coordinate factors.
- **claim-relative-translation-koszul** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-translation-descent)): On the cohomology rows in <a href="#eq:boundary-split-cohomology" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:boundary-split-cohomology">[eq:boundary-split-cohomology]</a>, some subgroup $T'_h=[p]^hT'$ acts trivially. Over an Artin parameter neighborhood, write $$\Lambda_N=R_N[[D_1,\ldots,D_\delta]], \qquad \delta=e_s(s-1),\qquad I=(D_1,\ldots,D_\delta)$$ for the distribution algebra of $T'_h$, transported along $T'\simeq T'_h$. If $V$ is a row with trivial $T'_h$ action, then $$\label{eq:boundary-relative-koszul} H^j(T'_h,V) \simeq V\otimes_{R_N}\bigwedge^j(I/I^2)^\vee, \qquad 0\leq j\leq\delta.$$ This description is functorial under changes of distribution coordinates and under all the commuting actions.
  - Explanation: Scalar conjugation forces a uniform deep relative translation subgroup to act trivially; its row cohomology is the exterior augmentation-conormal calculation.
- **claim-individual-row-finiteness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-boundary-row-finiteness)): Let $V$ be a torsion-free pro-$p$ compact $p$-adic analytic group, and let $C$ be a bounded complex of smooth $k[V]$-modules. If $R\Gamma(V,C)$ has finite-dimensional cohomology in each degree, then $$H^a(V,H^i(C))$$ is finite-dimensional for every $a,i$. These groups are zero outside finitely many $(a,i)$ when $C$ has bounded cohomology.
  - Explanation: Finite total derived invariants force finite-dimensional individual rows through pseudocompact duality and finite generation over the completed group algebra.
- **claim-stable-lattice-cutoff** (theorem, [source](#stmt-full-stable-cutoff)): At a sufficiently deep fixed frame level, let $P=x^{-b}L$ be a transfer-stable compact lattice as in Proposition <a href="#prop:transpose-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:transpose-comparison">29</a>. The map $$H^i(P_n,P)\longrightarrow H^i(P_n,B_U)$$ identifies the stable images of transfer on its source and target. Consequently the transpose comparison remains valid when the compact lattice is replaced by the entire bounded-pole coefficient. The resulting comparison of dual direct-limit complexes preserves constant stabilizer cochains and finite-level trace maps.
  - Explanation: After finiteness, compact and localized coefficient cohomology have identical stable transfer images and equivalent dual colimits with their actions.
- **claim-dual-complex-trace-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-full-trace-descent)): Let $U=K\times V$. There is a natural equivalence $$\label{full:dual-descent} R\Gamma\bigl(U,R\Gamma(T_h,\mathcal D)\bigr) \simeq C^\bullet(P_n,B_{K,V}^{(h)})^*,$$ where $B_{K,V}^{(h)}$ denotes the corresponding lift/root coefficient. Taking $h=0$ means the trivial translation representation. The equivalence is compatible with transpose cup actions. Under it, corestriction in $K$ or $V$ is dual to pullback of bounded-pole coefficients. Power transport identifies the questions about $B_{K,V}^{(h)}$ with those about $B_{K,V}$, retaining ordinary $\mathbb F_p$-cochains.
  - Explanation: Translation and frame invariants recover dual bounded-pole cochains; frame corestriction is dual to coefficient pullback.
- **claim-full-frame-support-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-full-frame-comparison)): Let $R=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi)^a$, with $\varpi=p^\flat$, and let $Z=(N_t^m)_{\mathrm{ind}}$ be the independent extension locus of Theorem <a href="#thm:geometric-quotient" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:geometric-quotient">19</a>. Use the geometric coefficient $\mathscr A=(\mathcal O^{\flat,+}/\varpi)^a$ of Section <a href="#sec:support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:support">5</a>. There is an equivalence $$\label{full:eq-three} \mathcal D\otimes_k R \simeq R\Gamma_c(Z;\mathscr A)\otimes\langle\eta\rangle[m+n^2]$$ after forgetting translations. It is $U_0$-equivariant and linear for the action of ordinary constant stabilizer cochains. It is also compatible with all finite-frame trace maps used in Lemma <a href="#full:trace-descent" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:trace-descent">42</a>.
  - Explanation: After forgetting translations, the full dual complex is equivariantly identified with compact supports and the retained volume shift.
- **claim-scalar-deep-translation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-full-scalar-translation)): Let $M$ be a rational $T$-representation with a compatible action of a scalar $a\in1+p\mathbb Z_p$, $a\ne1$, conjugating $T$ by multiplication by $a$ or $a^{-1}$. If $a$ acts as the identity on $M$, then $T_h$ acts trivially on $M$ for sufficiently large $h$. A single $h$ works for a family of such modules on which this same scalar is the identity.
  - Explanation: An identity scalar compatible with translation conjugation forces sufficiently deep translations to act trivially, uniformly across modules sharing that scalar.
- **claim-connected-corestriction-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-full-corestriction)): Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth $k$-representation of $P_t$. For a cofinal sequence of sufficiently small compact open subgroups $K\subset P_t$, inverse limit with corestriction gives $$\varprojlim_{K,\mathrm{cor}} H^c(K,M)=0\quad(c\ne t^2), \qquad \varprojlim_{K,\mathrm{cor}} H^{t^2}(K,M)\simeq M.$$ The last isomorphism uses a fixed orientation and is natural for commuting endomorphisms of $M$. More generally, for a bounded smooth $P_t$-complex $C$ with finite-dimensional cohomology, it gives $$\label{full:connected-complex-limit} \varprojlim_{K,\mathrm{cor}} H^\ell\bigl(R\Gamma(K,C)\bigr) \simeq H^{\ell-t^2}(C).$$ This identification is natural for maps of coefficient complexes, including degree-shifted maps. Normal connected levels retain the commuting actions and the action of $P_t$ by conjugation.
  - Explanation: Connected-frame corestriction limits retain only the oriented top group degree, naturally for bounded coefficient complexes and shifted maps.
- **claim-full-frame-induction-completion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-full-joint-completion)): For every compact open $V\subset G$, the graded vector space $$H^*(P_n,B_{\mathrm{conn},V})$$ has finite total dimension. There is an integer $e$, depending on $(n,t)$, such that the scalar subgroup $1+p^e\mathbb Z_p\subset G$ acts identically on $H^*(P_n,B_{\mathrm{full}})$. The same scalar subgroup acts identically after adjoining the algebraic union of Frobenius roots. Together with Proposition <a href="#full:perfected-row-characters" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:perfected-row-characters">50</a> below, these statements complete the full-frame part of Theorem <a href="#thm:coefficient-finiteness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:coefficient-finiteness">13</a> at the current induction step.
  - Explanation: Proves connected-frame finiteness at every fixed matrix level and a uniform scalar identity on the full algebraic frame and root unions.
- **claim-root-inclusion-corestriction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-full-root-corestriction)): In the equivalence of Lemma <a href="#full:trace-descent" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:trace-descent">42</a>, the transpose of the inclusion $B_{K,V}^{(h)}\hookrightarrow B_{K,V}^{(h')}$ for $h'>h$ is finite-Hopf corestriction $$R\Gamma(T_{h'},\mathcal D)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_h,\mathcal D).$$ This identification commutes with the compact frame-group corestrictions and with the action of $P_s$ by conjugation on normal connected levels.* *Suppose $s>1$, and suppose $T_h$ acts trivially on every $H^j(\mathcal D)$. On a cohomology row the displayed transition is zero in translation degrees $b<d$ and is the oriented identity in degree $d$, up to a nonzero normalization scalar.
  - Explanation: Actual root inclusions transpose to translation corestriction; on trivial rows the transitions kill lower translation degrees and preserve the top orientation.
- **claim-perfected-connected-character-test** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-full-perfected-connected-calculation)): Choose $h_0$ so that $T_{h_0}$ acts trivially on $H^*(\mathcal D)$, and set $A_h=R\Gamma(V,R\Gamma(T_h,\mathcal D))$. For every compact open $V\subset G$, there are natural $P_s$-equivariant identifications $$\label{full:perfected-connected-dual} \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_k\!\left( H^i(P_n,B_{\mathrm{conn},V}^{\mathrm{perf}}),k\right) \ \simeq\ \varprojlim_{h,\operatorname{cor}} H^{-i-s^2}(A_h).$$ All vector spaces in this formula are finite dimensional. Let $\chi$ be a character of $\Delta_s$. If $$\label{full:top-row-character-test} H^a(V,H^q(\mathcal D)\otimes E_h^d)_\chi=0 \quad\text{for every }a,q\text{ and }h\geq h_0,$$ then the $\chi$-isotypic part of the dual in <a href="#full:perfected-connected-dual" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="full:perfected-connected-dual">[full:perfected-connected-dual]</a> is zero. For $s=1$, put $d=0$ and $E_h^0=k$.
  - Explanation: Finite inverse corestriction systems compute the perfected connected dual and detect character vanishing from top translation rows without formality.
- **claim-perfected-tame-norm-characters** (classification, [source](#stmt-full-perfected-support-characters)): The $P_s$-action on $H^i(P_n,B_{\mathrm{conn},V}^{\mathrm{perf}})$ has only norm characters on $\Delta_s$, for every $i$ and every compact open $V\subset G$.
  - Explanation: The perfected connected-frame cohomology has only tame norm characters after volume and top translation characters combine.
- **claim-perfected-row-norm-filtration** (classification, [source](#stmt-full-perfected-row-characters)): At the current induction pair $(n,s)$, for every compact open $V\subset\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_{n-s}(\mathbb Z_p)$ and all $a,i$, the vector space $$Q=H^a\!\left(V, H^i(P_n,B_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{perf}})\right)$$ is finite dimensional and has a finite $P_s$-stable filtration whose successive quotients are one-dimensional characters $\nu_s^j$. Its dual has a filtration by the inverse characters. This assertion concerns the representations arising from these perfected full-frame rows.
  - Explanation: Individual perfected full-frame matrix-cohomology rows are finite and admit stabilizer-stable filtrations by norm characters, with inverse filtrations on duals.
- **claim-integral-constant-cohomology** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-constant-cohomology)): For $G=K_a,I_a$, or $P_a$, the groups $H^q(G,\mathbb Z_p)$ are finite free $\mathbb Z_p$-modules, vanish for $q>a^2$, and have Poincaré polynomial $$\sum_q\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z_p}H^q(G,\mathbb Z_p)z^q =\prod_{i=1}^a(1+z^{2i-1}). \label{eq:const-poincare}$$ There are exterior-algebra presentations over $\mathbb Z_p$, and over every finite extension of $\mathbb F_p$, with generators in degrees $2i-1$, $1\leq i\leq a$. For every $r\geq1$, reduction induces an isomorphism $$H^q(G,\mathbb Z_p)/p^r\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^q(G,\mathbb Z/p^r). \label{eq:const-reduction}$$ The actual restriction maps $$H^*(K_a,\mathbb Z_p)\longrightarrow H^*(I_a,\mathbb Z_p),\qquad H^*(K_a,\mathbb Z/p^r)\longrightarrow H^*(I_a,\mathbb Z/p^r)$$ are isomorphisms. These assertions do not select the generators: the compatible stable generators will be constructed in Theorem <a href="#thm:stable-generators" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:stable-generators">56</a>.
  - Explanation: Computes integral and finite constant cohomology as exterior algebras, with torsion-free reduction and actual matrix-to-Iwahori restriction isomorphisms.
- **claim-building-restriction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-const-building)): Restriction along $K_a\subset J_a$ induces an equivalence $$C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(J_a;E)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(K_a;E)$$ for every finite Postnikov $p$-primary constant coefficient spectrum $E$. It also induces isomorphisms with constant coefficients $\mathbb Z_p$ and $\mathbb Z/p^r$.
  - Explanation: The determinant-valuation-zero group and its maximal compact subgroup have equivalent finite Postnikov constant cochains by actual restriction.
- **claim-common-modification-stack** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-const-modification-stack)): There is a common modification stack, with its determinant lattice, $$\mathcal M_n\simeq[\mathbb P^{n-1}_C/P_n] \simeq[\Omega^{n-1}_C/J_n]. \label{eq:const-modification-stack}$$ The two presentations commute with the arithmetic action over $K$. In particular, arithmetic acts trivially on the continuous group cochains of $P_n$ and $J_n$. Their structural maps to geometric cochains, constructed in the next subsection, are arithmetic-equivariant.
  - Explanation: Constructs determinant-matched division and split presentations of a common modification stack with compatible arithmetic actions.
- **claim-actual-constant-transport** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-modification-transport)): The structural maps from <a href="#eq:const-modification-stack" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:const-modification-stack">[eq:const-modification-stack]</a> identify $$H^*(P_n,\mathbb F_p)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^*(\mathcal M_n,\mathbb F_p)_{(1)} \xleftarrow{\ \sim\ }H^*(J_n,\mathbb F_p), \label{eq:const-weight-zero}$$ where $(1)$ denotes generalized eigenvalue one for $\gamma$. These are identifications by the actual pullback maps and preserve cup products. Together with Lemma <a href="#lem:const-building" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:const-building">53</a>, they induce natural equivalences, for every finite Postnikov $p$-primary spectrum $E$, $$C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;E)\ \simeq\ C^*(\mathcal M_n;E)_{(1)}\ \simeq\ C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(J_n;E)\ \simeq\ C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(K_n;E). \label{eq:const-postnikov-transport}$$ The equivalences commute with coefficient maps, products, and Hurewicz maps. They extend to the $p$-complete sphere by the Postnikov and coefficient limits defining continuous cochains.* *There is also the following compatibility on the independent extension locus $Z=(N_t^m)_{\mathrm{ind}}$, $m=n-t$. After fixing the connected quotient frame, let $$b:[Z/K_m]\longrightarrow BP_n,\qquad q:[Z/K_m]\longrightarrow BK_m$$ be the positive middle-bundle classifying map and the structural map. If $c_P$ and $c_K$ correspond under <a href="#eq:const-postnikov-transport" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:const-postnikov-transport">[eq:const-postnikov-transport]</a>, then $$b^*c_P=q^*\operatorname{res}_{K_m}^{K_n}(c_K), \qquad K_m\longrightarrow K_n,\quad g\longmapsto\operatorname{diag}(g,1_t). \label{eq:const-block-action}$$ This equality holds for finite Postnikov coefficients, for their stable limits, and for the resulting ordinary cup actions. In particular the constant action in Proposition <a href="#prop:full-frame-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:full-frame-comparison">43</a> is the actual block-restriction action.
  - Explanation: Arithmetic separation transports actual constant cochains and sphere representatives through modification, identifying their extension-space action with block restriction.
- **claim-stable-primitive-generators** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-stable-generators)): Let $1\leq N\leq p-2$. There are classes $$c_{a,i}\in \pi_{1-2i}C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a;S), \qquad 1\leq i\leq a\leq N,$$ with leading integral classes $$\alpha_{a,i}\in H^{2i-1}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a,\mathbb Z_p),$$ having the following properties.* 1. *The classes $\alpha_{a,i}$ induce isomorphisms of graded algebras $$\bigwedge_{\mathbb Z_p}(\alpha_{a,1},\ldots,\alpha_{a,a}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a,\mathbb Z_p), \qquad \bigwedge_{\mathbb F_p}(\overline\alpha_{a,1},\ldots, \overline\alpha_{a,a}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a,\mathbb F_p).$$ Their rationalizations are nonzero multiples of the standard primitive classes. For $i=1$ the class is the divided determinant logarithm.* 2. *For the upper-left block inclusion $G_b\longrightarrow G_a$, with $b\leq a$, one has $$\operatorname{res}\alpha_{a,i}=\alpha_{b,i}\quad(i\leq b), \qquad \operatorname{res}\alpha_{a,i}=0\quad(b<i\leq a).$$ The sphere representatives can be chosen so that $\operatorname{res}c_{a,i}=c_{b,i}$ for $i\leq b$.* 3. *Apply Proposition <a href="#prop:modification-transport" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:modification-transport">55</a> at rank $N$. The classes $c_{N,i}$ have transported representatives $$u_i\in\pi_{1-2i}C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_N;S).$$ Their leading mod-$p$ classes, denoted $\xi_i$, are the transported classes $\overline\alpha_{N,i}$. On the extension space with a marked connected quotient and an $m$-dimensional Tate kernel, their constant cohomology action is the upper-left block restriction of $\overline\alpha_{N,i}$, hence is given by $\overline\alpha_{m,i}$ for $i\leq m$ and vanishes for $i>m$.
  - Explanation: Selects compatible sphere representatives whose leading integral and reduced classes are exterior generators and whose transported action is actual block restriction.
- **claim-continuous-standard-representation** (construction, [source](#stmt-gen-k-continuity)): The classes $\kappa_{a,r}$ define a continuous additive class $$\kappa_a\in \pi_0 C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a;K(\mathbb Z_p)^\wedge_p).$$ If $f:K(\mathbb Z_p)^\wedge_p\longrightarrow E$ is a map to a complete connective spectrum of finite type, composition with $f$ is represented in the continuous Postnikov cochain construction. It is compatible with restriction to blocks and with block sums. Restriction to the discrete group $G_a$ agrees with evaluation of the usual discrete algebraic $K$-theory class followed by completion and $f$.
  - Explanation: Finite standard-representation classes define a continuous additive completed K-theory class compatible with blocks, composition, and discrete evaluation.
- **claim-local-k-coordinate-projections** (construction, [source](#stmt-gen-local-k-coordinates)): For $2\leq i\leq p-2$, there are spectrum maps $$f_i:K(\mathbb Z_p)^\wedge_p\longrightarrow\Sigma^{2i-1}\ell_p$$ which induce a generator coordinate on the free group in degree $2i-1$. Via the integral etale edge and localization for $\mathbb Q_p$, this coordinate identifies that group with $H^1(\mathbb Q_p,\mathbb Z_p(i))$, up to a $p$-adic unit.
  - Explanation: Local K-theory admits selected Adams-summand coordinates identifying the relevant free homotopy group with integral local Galois cohomology up to a unit.
- **claim-rational-additive-components** (classification, [source](#stmt-gen-rational-components)): For $a\leq p-2$ and $i\leq a$, the only possibly nonzero rational ordinary-cohomology component of $z_{a,i}$ is its component in degree $2i-1$. Moreover $\alpha_{a,i}\otimes\mathbb Q_p$ is a scalar multiple of $b_i$.
  - Explanation: Stable additivity eliminates higher rational ordinary components and places the leading class in the standard primitive line.
- **claim-spherical-primitive-lifts** (construction, [source](#stmt-gen-sphere-representatives)): For $1\leq i\leq a\leq p-2$, the class $\alpha_{a,i}$ has a representative in $\pi_{1-2i}C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_a;S)$. For $i\geq2$ its image in $\ell_p$ is $z_{a,i}$. For $i=1$ one can take the pullback of the divided logarithm along the determinant.
  - Explanation: The selected leading classes lift through the connective image of J to sphere cochains in the stated rank range; the logarithmic class supplies the first generator.
- **claim-integral-soule-coordinate** (construction, [source](#stmt-gen-soule-coordinate)): Let $2\leq i\leq p-2$, $d=2i-1$, and $X=K(\mathbb Z_p)^\wedge_p$. There is a $\mathbb Z_p$-linear isomorphism $$c_i^{\mathrm S}:\pi_dX\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(\mathbb Q_p,\mathbb Z_p(i))$$ whose value on the completion of $x\in K_d(\mathbb Z_p)$ rationalizes to the Soulé regulator $r_p(x)$ of (Huber and Kings 2011, sec. 1.3) [[HuberKings](#ref-HuberKings)], restricted from $\mathbb Q_p$ by localization.
  - Explanation: An integral universal Chern coordinate is an isomorphism and agrees on completed discrete classes with the rational Soulé regulator.
- **claim-integral-exponential-lattice** (classification, [source](#stmt-gen-exponential-lattice)): For $2\leq i\leq p-2$, use the standard period basis to identify $D_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathbb Q_p(i))$ with $\mathbb Q_p$. Then $$\exp_{\mathrm{BK}}^{-1} H^1(\mathbb Q_p,\mathbb Z_p(i))=p^i\mathbb Z_p.$$
  - Explanation: Determines the exact integral local Galois lattice in the standard de Rham period coordinate.
- **claim-discrete-regulator-detected** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gen-detected-regulator)): For $2\leq i\leq p-2$, the Soulé regulator $$r_p:K_{2i-1}(\mathbb Z_p)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q_p \longrightarrow H^1(\mathbb Q_p,\mathbb Q_p(i))$$ is nonzero.
  - Explanation: A root-of-unity polylogarithmic class detects a nonzero discrete Soulé regulator, enabling scalar normalization by an actual evaluation.
- **claim-selected-primitive-normalization** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-regulator-lattice)): With the choices of Lemma <a href="#gen:local-k-coordinates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="gen:local-k-coordinates">58</a>, there are units $\varepsilon_i\in\mathbb Z_p^\times$, independent of the matrix rank, such that $$\label{gen:primitive-normalization} \alpha_{a,i}\otimes\mathbb Q_p=\varepsilon_i p^{-i}b_i \qquad (2\leq i\leq a\leq p-2).$$ The same formula holds for $i=1$, with a unit $\varepsilon_1$ determined by the divided logarithm.
  - Explanation: Normalizes the selected primitive classes by the integral exponential lattice and a detected regulator evaluation, with units independent of rank.
- **claim-top-integral-volume-lattice** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-top-volume)): Assume $a\leq p-2$.* 1. *In rational Lie algebra cohomology, $$b_1\wedge\cdots\wedge b_a=u_a\omega_a, \qquad u_a\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}^\times.$$* 2. *For all sufficiently large integers $r$, the integral top cohomology lattice of $U_r=1+p^rM_a(\mathbb Z_p)$ corresponds under the rational Lazard comparison to $$\mathbb Z_p\,p^{-rd}\omega_a.$$* 3. *The top integral lattice of $G_a$ corresponds to $$\mathbb Z_p\,p^{-a(a+1)/2}\omega_a.$$
  - Explanation: Computes the primitive product volume and integral top lattices for deep congruence subgroups and the full matrix group.
- **claim-parabolic-weight-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-weight-vanishing)): For every $a,q,b$ one has $$\label{full:weight-vanishing} H^a\bigl(G,H_c^q(Z;\mathscr A)\otimes \langle\eta\rangle\otimes E_h^b\bigr)=0$$ unless $q=(t+2)m$ and $b=d$. For $b=d$, extension to the ambient space induces an equivalence $$\label{full:ambient-edge} \begin{aligned} &R\Gamma\bigl(G,R\Gamma_c(Z;\mathscr A)\otimes \langle\eta\rangle\otimes E_h^d\bigr)\\ &\qquad\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } R\Gamma\bigl(G,R\Gamma_c(N_t^m;\mathscr A)\otimes \langle\eta\rangle\otimes E_h^d\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ The remaining ambient coefficient is a line with trivial $G$-action. All assertions preserve the commuting connected-frame action.
  - Explanation: Finite-torus weight bounds eliminate proper-plane support terms and lower translation degrees, leaving a trivial ambient matrix coefficient line.
- **claim-equivariant-top-edge** (construction, [source](#stmt-full-top-edge)): There is a natural $U_0$-equivariant map $$\label{full:top-edge-map} \mathcal D\otimes_k E_h^d[-d]\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_h,\mathcal D).$$ On a trivially acted-on cohomology row, it is insertion into translation degree $d$. The map is linear for constant stabilizer cochains. After applying $R\Gamma(G,-)$ it is an equivalence, as a complex with the remaining smooth $P_t$-action.
  - Explanation: Canonical local duality gives a top translation insertion even for a derived translation action; matrix invariants make it an equivalence.
- **claim-surviving-constant-action** (classification, [source](#stmt-full-surviving-module)): After tensoring with $R$ and choosing the one-dimensional orientation factors, there are graded identifications $$\label{full:dual-poincare-module} \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_k(M_t^i,k)\otimes_kR \simeq A_G^{m^2-i}\otimes_kR.$$ If a constant class on $P_n$ corresponds to a class on $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_n(\mathbb Z_p)$ under Proposition <a href="#prop:modification-transport" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:modification-transport">55</a>, its transpose action on the right of <a href="#full:dual-poincare-module" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="full:dual-poincare-module">[full:dual-poincare-module]</a> is ordinary cup product by the upper-left block restriction of that class to $G$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the regraded coefficient dual with matrix constant cohomology and identifies the actual transpose action with block-restricted cup product.
- **claim-unit-generated-exterior-module** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-constant-module)): For $1\leq t<n<p-1$, put $m=n-t$. The cup map $$\label{full:constant-basis} \bigwedge_k(e_1,\ldots,e_m) \longrightarrow H^*(P_n,B_{\mathrm{conn},G}), \qquad e_i\longmapsto \xi_i\cdot1,\qquad \|e_i\|=2i-1,$$ is an isomorphism of graded $k$-algebras. In particular, for $I\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}$ the products $$\xi_I\cdot1=\left(\prod_{i\in I}\xi_i\right)\cdot1$$ form a basis in cohomological degrees $\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1)$ and internal degree zero. The classes $\xi_i$ for $i>m$ act as zero. The assertion uses the fixed rank-$n$ classes simultaneously for every $t$.
  - Explanation: The coefficient unit generates the specified exterior algebra under the common rank family, while higher-index constants act trivially.
- **claim-universal-exact-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-spec-exact-descent)): The augmentation $D\to\operatorname{Tot}\mathcal A^\bullet$ is an equivalence. Moreover, if $F$ is an exact functor from spectra to a stable $\infty$-category admitting countable limits, then $$F(D)\xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;} \operatorname{Tot}\bigl(F(\mathcal A^\bullet)\bigr). \label{spec:exact-totalization}$$ The transformed partial-totalization tower is quickly convergent. For spectrum-valued $F$, its totalization spectral sequence has this convergence control. In particular, if its $E_2$-page lies in a bounded range of cohomological degrees, it converges strongly with a finite filtration in each total degree.
  - Explanation: Quick convergence of completed Morava descent makes its totalization invariant under exact functors and supplies bounded-page strong convergence.
- **claim-common-global-sphere-classes** (construction, [source](#stmt-spec-global-classes)): There are classes $$y_i\in\pi_{1-2i}D,\qquad 1\leq i\leq n,$$ represented by constant sphere-cochain classes whose integral Hurewicz images on $P_n$ are $\alpha^P_{n,i}$. For $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_r\}$, put $$y_I=y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_r},\qquad y_\varnothing=1.$$ These are represented by actual sphere-cochain classes with Hurewicz image $\alpha^P_{n,i_1}\cdots\alpha^P_{n,i_r}$. The class $y_\varnothing$ is the unit $S\to D$.
  - Explanation: Averaged constant sphere cochains define common classes in the local sphere, with prescribed integral Hurewicz images and the actual unit as empty product.
- **claim-flat-completed-function-modules** (theorem, [source](#stmt-spec-flat-functions)): Let $R=W(k)[[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]]$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $Q$ be a profinite set. The module $N_Q=C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,R)$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete and flat over $R$. Its reductions are $$N_Q/\mathfrak m^aN_Q =C_{\mathrm{lc}}(Q,R/\mathfrak m^a).$$ Quotienting by $p,x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}$ gives $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,A)$.
  - Explanation: Continuous functions into the deformation ring are complete and flat, with reduction and height quotients computed by continuous coefficient division.
- **claim-ordinary-residue-cobar** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ordinary-residue)): For the completed terms $\mathcal A^\bullet$ in <a href="#spec:amitsur" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="spec:amitsur">[spec:amitsur]</a>, followed by ordinary smash with $\kappa_t$, there is a natural quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes $$N^*\pi_r(\kappa_t\wedge\mathcal A^\bullet) \simeq \kappa_{t,r}\otimes_k C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;\mathcal B_{n,t}). \label{spec:residue-complex}$$ Here $N^*$ denotes normalization of a cosimplicial abelian group. The right side uses one finite algebraic connected-marking stage and one bound on the pole order on each compact cochain domain. It is zero when $r$ is odd. The comparison carries the unit to $1$ and the constant-cochain action to the actual constant cup action of Proposition <a href="#prop:constant-module" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:constant-module">69</a>.
  - Explanation: Ordinary residue smash of completed descent recovers algebraic connected-marking cochains with bounded poles, including the actual semilinear coface and constant action.
- **claim-simultaneous-lower-height-bases** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-height-bases)): The common classes of Proposition <a href="#spec:global-classes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="spec:global-classes">71</a> satisfy, for every $1\leq t<n$, $$L_{K(t)}\left( \bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}} \Sigma^{-d(I)}S\xrightarrow{(y_I)}D \right) \quad\text{is an equivalence}, \label{spec:height-basis}$$ where $d(I)=\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1)$, and the empty component is the unit.
  - Explanation: The actual products of the common sphere classes lift every residue basis vector through descent and induce all required lower-height equivalences.
- **claim-rational-local-sphere** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-rational-sphere)): For every prime $p$ and height $n\geq1$, the rational homotopy of the $K(n)$-local sphere is the exterior $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra $$\pi_*L_{K(n)}S\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q \cong\bigwedge_{\mathbb Q_p}(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_n), \qquad \|\zeta_i\|=1-2i,$$ with its natural scalar action induced by the unit. In particular, $$\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}L_0D =\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\} \qquad(b\in\mathbb Z). \label{spec:rational-dimensions}$$
  - Explanation: The rational local sphere has exterior homotopy, supplying the independent rational dimension count used for the final filtration block.

        "exact_quote": "The rings $B_U$ form a tower of finite étale $B$-algebras.         "anchor": "stmt-rings-coinduction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $r$ be one of the chosen levels and put $H=[p]^rT$. Transport a finite $T$-representation $M$ to $H$ using $[p]^r:T\\simeq H$, and then coinduce it to $T$. This is an exact functor, denoted $\\mathcal C_r$. There is a natural $P_n$- and auxiliary-equivariant identification of the associated coefficient diagram for $\\mathcal C_rM$ with the $Q$-root version of the diagram for $M$. Powering by $Q$ identifies the two diagrams $k$-linearly and Frobenius-semilinearly over the base: $$\\label{rings:power-scalar-rule}\n \\Phi_Q(cf)=c^Q\\Phi_Q(f),\\qquad \\Phi_Q(f)=f^Q.$$ The assertion holds for every morphism and every finite diagram, and after invariants in any compatible open frame subgroup.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-cartier-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Fix one sufficiently divisible step with function-root exponent $Q$, and use the volume just constructed. The quotient transfers of the lift torsors can be normalized compatibly so that, after powering to a fixed finite frame ring, their first step is $$\\label{rings:stationary-c}\n S(f)=\\frac{\\mathscr C_Q(f\\eta)}{\\eta},$$ where $\\mathscr C_Q$ is Cartier trace on continuous top differentials. The subsequent stationary transfers are $S^a$. In particular $S(c^Qf)=cS(f)$.*\n\n*These transfers are finite Hopf integration on the torsor, not ordinary field trace. They commute with $P_n$, with their natural auxiliary actions, and with finite étale change of frame level. Their transpose under the residue pairing is positive Frobenius on dual coefficient functions, with the one volume line <a href=\"#rings:volume-character\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"rings:volume-character\">[rings:volume-character]</a> retained. Before stationary identification it is the inclusion into the next root coefficient ring. For a finite étale cover or its associated coefficient module, this is the actual Frobenius on the cover functions and their trace duals. All statements hold for finite diagrams in Lemma <a href=\"#rings:coinduction\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"rings:coinduction\">10</a>.",

        "anchor": "stmt-thm-coefficient-finiteness",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $1\\leq t<n<p-1$. The following assertions hold.*\n\n1.  *Every admissible compact coefficient on $A$ or $C_1$ has finite total continuous $P_n$-cohomology. This includes the stable finite free lattices constructed below.*\n\n2.  *For every finite joint frame level $U$, the bounded-pole groups $H^*(P_n,B_U)$ have finite total dimension. The assertion also holds with a fixed power of the invariant line. Finite direct sums and finite-dimensional trivial coefficient factors are allowed.*\n\n3.  *For every fixed compact open $V\\subset\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_m(\\mathbb Z_p)$, $H^*(P_n,B_{\\mathrm{conn},V})$ has finite total dimension. There is an integer $h$, independent of the rectangular levels used in the union, such that $1+p^h\\mathbb Z_p$ acting by scalar matrices acts identically on $H^*(P_n,B_{\\mathrm{full}})$. These conclusions persist after taking the algebraic union of Frobenius roots, with the actions transported by powering.*\n\n    *Moreover, put $B_{\\mathrm{full}}^{\\mathrm{perf}}\n     =\\mathop{\\mathrm{colim}}_r B_{\\mathrm{full}}^{1/p^r}$, the algebraic root union with common finite stages on compact cochain sources.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-compact-norm-line",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal G$ be the algebraic height-$s$, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group obtained from the universal formal deformation, and let $\\mathcal R_s$ be its characteristic-$p$ complete local deformation ring. There is a functorial height-one, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group $$\\mathcal H_{\\det}=\\bigwedge^s\\mathcal G.$$ Its marked deformation is canonically constant. The covariant action of $P_s$ on its special group, and hence on this constant marked deformation, is multiplication by the actual unit $\\operatorname{Nrd}(g)\\in\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$.*\n\n*With the convention that actions on functions use inverse substitution, put $$\\mathcal N_s=\n       \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathcal R_s}(\\omega_{\\mathcal H_{\\det}},\\mathcal R_s).$$ Then there is a $P_s$-equivariant identification $$\\mathcal N_s\\simeq\n                 \\mathcal R_s\\otimes_k k(\\nu_s).$$ Every integral tensor power of this line is admissible on every starting-height quotient of the deformation disc and on its labeled disc.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-compact-stable-lattices",
        "exact_quote": "At a sufficiently deep finite joint frame level, the finite free coefficient $B_U$ and the associated coefficients of any fixed finite translation diagram admit $P_n$-stable free $C_1$-lattices. Their fixed pole strips have finite filtrations by boundary restrictions of admissible coefficients. For the stationary functions coefficient one can choose such a lattice $L$ and an integer $b$ so that $$P=x^{-b}L$$ is preserved by $S$, and every $x^{-c}L$ is carried into $P$ by a sufficiently high iterate of $S$. In the invariant-volume frames the transpose on the dual lattice of top forms has Frobenius matrix entries in $xC_1$. Its finite basis, viewed as finite-cover functions by these frames, can be taken integral over $C_1$.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $L$ be a stable finite free lattice over a formal $r$-disc $C$, and let $\\mathfrak m_C$ be its closed-point ideal.         "exact_quote": "Let $K$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group without $p$-torsion, and put $R_K=\\mathbb F_p[[K]]$.       "conclusion": {

        "exact_quote": "Let $U=K\\times V$.         "exact_quote": "Let $1\\leq N\\leq p-2$. For $i=1$ the class is the divided determinant logarithm.*\n\n2.  *For the upper-left block inclusion $G_b\\longrightarrow G_a$, with $b\\leq a$, one has $$\\operatorname{res}\\alpha_{a,i}=\\alpha_{b,i}\\quad(i\\leq b),\n     \\qquad\n     \\operatorname{res}\\alpha_{a,i}=0\\quad(b<i\\leq a).$$ The sphere representatives can be chosen so that $\\operatorname{res}c_{a,i}=c_{b,i}$ for $i\\leq b$.*\n\n3.  *Apply Proposition <a href=\"#prop:modification-transport\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:modification-transport\">55</a> at rank $N$. On the extension space with a marked connected quotient and an $m$-dimensional Tate kernel, their constant cohomology action is the upper-left block restriction of $\\overline\\alpha_{N,i}$, hence is given by $\\overline\\alpha_{m,i}$ for $i\\leq m$ and vanishes for $i>m$.",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Completed sphere and local sphere** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Put $S=S_p^\wedge$ and $D=L_{K(n)}S$.
- **Subset suspension degree** ([source](#pm-h-8)): For a finite subset $I$ of the positive integers put $$d(I)=\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1),\qquad d(\varnothing)=0.$$
- **Chromatic overlap** ([source](#sec:introduction)): The fracture square relates height $n$ to the lower heights through the overlap $$X_{n,p}=L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge.$$
- **Bounded-pole common-stage cochains** ([source](#stmt-rings-bounded-cochains)): For a finite projective module over a finite frame algebra we use continuous cochains with bounded poles. On a compact profinite source this means that one power of $x$ places the entire image in a finite power-series lattice, where the cochain is continuous for the parameter-adic topology. For a union of frame, root, or associated-bundle coefficients, one common finite stage is required on each compact source. Equivalently the cochain complex of such a union is the filtered colimit of its finite-stage bounded-pole cochain complexes. These conventions also apply with an additional compact profinite parameter.
- **Admissible compact coefficient** ([source](#stmt-def-compact-admissible)): An admissible compact coefficient on $A$ or $C_1$ is a finite free module with continuous $P_n$-action satisfying the following condition on every successive labeled height stratum. After restriction to its exact-height open, and after a finite joint frame change and a fixed finite Frobenius root change, the module has a finite $P_n$-stable filtration whose graded pieces admit $P_n$-equivariant identifications with finite direct sums of the coefficient ring, with $P_n$ acting only on that ring. We call these identifications constant frames; any commuting auxiliary frame actions are retained. The filtration splits as a filtration of underlying modules. The same condition is required after restriction to each dead-label boundary disc and power-identification with its starting-height disc. For a module on $A$ the condition is checked after pullback to the labeled strata. We also allow the constant frames to require a finite level of the translation splitting torsor. Equivalently, before that last ascent the graded pieces may be associated to finite representations of a finite translation quotient. The condition must still hold on every successive boundary stratum. All actions, filtrations, and splittings use bounded poles on each exact-height open.
- **Joint frame group and markings** ([source](#pm-h-11)): A connected marking is an isomorphism $$\alpha:\Gamma_t\longrightarrow \mathcal G_B^0$$ of formal groups, and an étale marking is an integral basis $i:\mathbb Z_p^m\longrightarrow T_p\mathcal G_B^{\mathrm{et}}$.
- **Algebraic joint frame union** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Write $\mathcal B=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U B_U$ for the entire joint algebraic frame ring.
- **Rational translation representation** ([source](#rings:distribution-ring)): The category of rational representations of the affine group scheme $T$ is the category in which every vector belongs to a representation of a finite quotient of $T$.
- **Associated translation coefficient** ([source](#pm-h-13)): For a finite translation representation $M$, its associated coefficient module is $$\mathcal V(M)=(\mathcal E\otimes_k M)^T.$$
- **Independent bundle-extension locus** ([source](#pm-h-20)): A tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_m)$ belongs to $Z$ if the map $$\mathbb Q_p^m\longrightarrow N_t,\qquad (a_1,\ldots,a_m)\longmapsto\sum_i a_i e_i$$ is injective at every geometric point.
- **Buffered compact-support convention** ([source](#pm-h-22)): All supports below are computed on bounded closed subdomains lying overconvergently inside an open chart.
- **Rational flag complex** ([source](#support:flag-complex-definition)): For a coefficient module $M$, consider the augmented complex $$\label{support:flag-complex-definition} \mathcal B_Q^a(M)= \bigoplus_{\substack{I\subset\Delta_s\\\|I\|=a-1}} \operatorname{LC}(\operatorname{Fl}_I(Q),M), \qquad 1\leq a\leq s.$$
- **Steinberg quotient** ([source](#support:flag-complex-definition)): Define $$\operatorname{St}(Q;M)= \frac{\operatorname{LC}(\operatorname{Fl}_{\Delta_s}(Q),M)} {\displaystyle\sum_{i\in\Delta_s} \operatorname{LC}(\operatorname{Fl}_{\Delta_s\setminus\{i\}}(Q),M)},$$ where the maps in the denominator are pullbacks.
- **Dual frame-and-translation complex** ([source](#full:dual-complex)): Take algebraic duals of the regular-representation complexes and form the filtered colimit over translation levels and joint frame levels: $$\label{full:dual-complex} \mathcal D=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{U,r} C_U^\bullet(N_r)^*.$$
- **Leading ordinary class** ([source](#gen:ahss)): We call this its leading ordinary class; it is defined even when it is zero.
- **Connected-marking coefficient for residue tests** ([source](#spec:connected-coefficients)): Here $K$ runs through open connected-marking levels.

| id | quantity | relation | value | regime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-generic-prime-range | prime p | > | $n+1$ | Positive height and prime in the stated generic range. |
| q-filtration-stage-count | number of individual filtration pieces | = | $2^n$ | The subset enumeration at the fixed height. |
| q-subset-suspension-degree | d(I) | = | $\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1)$ | Finite subsets, with the separately specified empty-subset convention. |
| q-universal-lift-rank | rank of the full universal lift algebra | = | $p^{tlm}$ | Finite torsion level and the stated height difference. |
| q-function-root-exponent | Q | = | $p^{tr}$ | The chosen divisible progression fixing the coefficient field. |
| q-distribution-frobenius-exponent | q | = | $p^{tr/(t-1)}$ | The same divisible progression as the function-root exponent. |
| q-finite-distribution-dimension | dimension of the finite distribution quotient | = | $q^d=Q^m$ | Chosen divisible translation levels. |
| q-compact-cohomology-upper-degree | nonvanishing compact lattice cohomology degree | ≤ | $n^2$ | The standing height and prime range. |
| q-affine-support-degree | cohomological degree of the affine support line | = | $2j$ | Affine dimension in the stated support comparison. |
| q-extension-power-support-degree | cohomological degree of the translation-quotient support line | = | $(t+2)j$ | The fixed connected height and the power of the extension sheaf. |
| q-proper-plane-support-degree | cohomological degree of a proper-plane contribution | = | $(t+2)j+(m-j)$ | Proper rational-plane dimensions in the displayed support formula. |
| q-transpose-comparison-shift | derived transpose comparison shift | = | $m+n^2$ | The fixed stable lattice and sufficiently deep finite frame level. |
| q-relative-translation-dimension | delta | = | $e_s(s-1)$ | The surviving étale rank and the Cartier-dual dimension. |
| q-constant-poincare-series | integral constant-cohomology rank series | = | $\prod_{i=1}^a(1+z^{2i-1})$ | Rank in the standing generic prime range. |
| q-first-beta-stem | first beta stem bounding sphere lifts | = | $2p(p-1)-2$ | The prime and rank used for continuous sphere representatives. |
| q-integral-exponential-lattice | inverse exponential image of integral local cohomology | = | $p^i\mathbb Z_p$ | The nonexceptional twist range specified in the lemma. |
| q-selected-primitive-scale | rationalized selected primitive | = | $\varepsilon_i p^{-i}b_i$ | Compatible coordinate choices across all permitted ranks. |
| q-full-group-top-lattice | top integral matrix-group cohomology lattice | = | $\mathbb Z_p\,p^{-a(a+1)/2}\omega_a$ | The matrix rank and its ordered entry-volume orientation. |
| q-primal-dual-degree | primal cohomological degree | = | $m^2-a$ | Matrix cohomological degree and the fixed height difference. |
| q-rational-subset-dimensions | rational homotopy dimension in degree minus b | = | $\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\}$ | Every integer degree at each positive height and prime. |

          "anchor": "full:degree-cancellation",
