## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-finite-rings** [claim](#stmt-prop-finite-rings) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-finite-rings): Generic full-basis factorization, regular local coordinates, finite-flat rank comparison, and Frobenius transition control. -> Finite labeled rings and unreduced lift schemes.
- **step-full-section-presentation** [claim](#stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation): Represent full tuples by finite norm identities and identify the regular complete local presentation. -> Integral full-section representability over nilpotent bases.
- **step-label-boundaries** [claim](#stmt-rings-boundary-labels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rings-boundary-labels): Factor the height coefficient and compare divided full-section polynomials after killing primitive labels. -> Higher-starting-height rooted boundary discs.
- **step-frame-torsors** [claim](#stmt-prop-frame-torsor) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-frame-torsor): Exact-height isomorphism towers and finite faithfully flat lift torsors. -> Joint frame tower with commuting actions and root lift algebras.
- **step-distribution-levels** [claim](#stmt-rings-dual-distribution) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rings-dual-distribution): Cartier duality and Honda Frobenius relations with normalized socle pairing. -> Compatible function-root and distribution exponents.
- **step-coinduction-powering** [claim](#stmt-rings-coinduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rings-coinduction): Coaction powering identity and finite coinduction descent. -> Natural equivariant powering on finite coefficient diagrams.
- **step-cartier-transpose** [claim](#stmt-lem-cartier-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cartier-transfer): Invariant-volume coefficient extraction and residue adjunction identify normalized Hopf integration and its transpose. -> Stationary Cartier transfer with actual Frobenius transpose.
- **step-norm-line** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-norm-line) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-norm-line): Top exterior Barsotti–Tate group, rigid height-one lifting, and determinant action. -> Admissible realization of reduced-norm character powers.
- **step-norm-filtered-extras** [claim](#stmt-cor-compact-norm-filtration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-compact-norm-filtration): Refine tensor filtrations using common finite determinant-line frames. -> Admissibility and conditional compact finiteness for tensor coefficients and duals.
- **step-stable-lattices** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-stable-lattices) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-stable-lattices): Triangular rescaling clears action denominators; inverse-semilinear estimates contract pole bounds and increase dual Frobenius positivity. -> Stable free lattices with controlled strips and integral positive dual functions.
- **step-compact-duality** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-duality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-duality): Finite profinite group resolutions, orientable analytic duality, and coordinate-independent residue pairing. -> Continuous duality and bounded compact cohomology.
- **step-tate-balls** [claim](#stmt-support-tate-ball) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-tate-ball): Uniform Honda-coordinate convergence and isometric density on bounded domains. -> Perfected Honda-ball model with rational independence locus.
- **step-geometric-quotient** [claim](#stmt-thm-geometric-quotient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-geometric-quotient): Relative slope classification, positive-section full faithfulness, determinant components, and additive presentation. -> Frame torsor over independent extensions and translation presentation of the extension sheaf.
- **step-solid-rows** [claim](#stmt-lem-solid-rows) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-solid-rows): Condense a finite projective profinite resolution and evaluate its finite retracts at a point. -> Finite row computation preserving scalar actions.
- **step-support-parameters** [claim](#stmt-support-parameters) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-parameters): Buffered integral continuity, finite clopen approximations, bounded group resolutions, and proper rational-plane incidence. -> Support descent and continuous smallest-plane maps.
- **step-affine-supports** [claim](#stmt-support-affine) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-affine): Primitive comparison on projective space and the hyperplane-complement localization fiber. -> Affine support line with natural affine action.
- **step-translation-supports** [claim](#stmt-support-translation-quotient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-translation-quotient): Exhaust translation quotients by buffered affine charts and take lattice Koszul corestriction limits. -> Extension-power support line with inverse lattice orientation.
- **step-flag-cohomology** [claim](#stmt-support-flag-complex) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-flag-complex): Bruhat filtration reduces each cell contribution to a signed Boolean complex. -> Top Steinberg quotient and lower-degree vanishing.
- **step-independent-supports** [claim](#stmt-prop-compact-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-compact-support): Proper plane incidence resolves dependence; smallest-plane contraction and flag cohomology determine the support spectral sequence. -> Explicit support rows and ambient top edge with retained incidence maps.
- **step-finite-support-invariants** [claim](#stmt-support-finite-invariants) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-finite-invariants): Finite flag resolutions, Shapiro, and finite analytic group resolutions bound almost length. -> Finite-range support invariants and finite-dimensional descent criterion.
- **step-principal-parts** [claim](#stmt-support-principal-parts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-principal-parts): Interleave genuine and buffered supports; norm-preserving Laurent Čech contraction leaves negative principal parts. -> Natural principal-parts comparison for the root colimit.
- **step-positive-extension** [claim](#stmt-support-positive-extension) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-positive-extension): Rooted intrinsic norm comparison on the puncture and boundary-zero transitions identify extension by zero. -> Almost equivalence with the punctured finite-cover coefficient extended by zero.
- **step-transpose-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-transpose-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-transpose-comparison): Compose group and residue duality, principal parts, positive extension, and the common torsor nerve. -> Derived support comparison preserving actual constant-cochain actions.
- **step-finite-stable-image** [claim](#stmt-support-finite-stable-image) / [proof](#proof-stmt-support-finite-stable-image): Faithful scalar extension and compact dual inverse limits identify the stable transfer intersection. -> Finite stable transfer image on compact lattice cohomology.
- **step-compact-operator** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-operator) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-operator): Nested compact fibers and a convergent power-series generation argument control stable images and nilpotent kernels. -> Finite kernel, finite cokernel, and comparison-intersection identity.
- **step-pro-constant** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-pro-constant) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-pro-constant): Descending cohomological induction through completed Koszul resolutions and the compact operator lemma. -> Constant regular translation pro-object with monic augmentation.
- **step-koszul-edge** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-koszul-edge) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-koszul-edge): Compare growing Koszul complexes and retain the leftmost edge after killing outgoing differentials. -> One fixed finite Yoneda extension giving the required epimorphism.

- **step-compact-finiteness** [claim](#stmt-prop-compact-finiteness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-compact-finiteness): Positive-lattice powered operations land in a finite transfer intersection; countability and compactness then force finiteness. -> Compact coefficient finiteness and localized countability at the current pair.
- **step-artin-splitting** [claim](#stmt-lem-artin-splitting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-artin-splitting): Triangular conormal comparison proves flatness; perfect special-fiber roots give the canonical Artin splitting. -> Canonical split Artin product with continuous common-stage cochains.

- **step-individual-row-finiteness** [claim](#stmt-boundary-row-finiteness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-row-finiteness): Pseudocompact duality, completed Nakayama, and Noetherian finite generation pass from total invariants to individual rows. -> Finite-dimensional matrix-group cohomology on each cohomology row.
- **step-pole-removal** [claim](#stmt-prop-pole-removal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-row-finiteness-2): Height-support filtration, Artin splitting, relative translation descent, matrix rows, and smaller-height compact duality. -> Finite total bounded-pole cohomology at every finite frame level.
- **step-stable-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-full-stable-cutoff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-stable-cutoff): Finite-dimensional stable-image decomposition and locally nilpotent comparison kernels replace compact coefficients by their localization. -> Equivalent dual transfer colimits preserving cup and trace maps.
- **step-trace-descent** [claim](#stmt-full-trace-descent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-trace-descent): Regular finite torsor modules give dual invariant acyclicity; exact associated-bundle tests yield translation injectivity. -> Dual bounded-pole cochains from frame and translation invariants.
- **step-full-support-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-full-frame-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-full-frame-comparison): Replace the compact cutoff and pass through all frame covers using transpose trace. -> Full dual complex identified with independent compact supports.
- **step-scalar-translations** [claim](#stmt-full-scalar-translation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-scalar-translation): Formal-group difference ideals or diagonalizable character decomposition detect deep translation triviality. -> Uniform deep translation subgroup acting trivially.
- **step-connected-corestriction** [claim](#stmt-full-corestriction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-corestriction): Orientable compact duality converts corestriction to restriction, whose positive-degree colimit vanishes. -> Top-degree connected inverse-limit calculation natural in shifted maps.
- **step-joint-completion** [claim](#stmt-full-joint-completion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-joint-completion): Support scalar symmetry, deep translation rows, finite flag invariants, and connected corestriction limits. -> Full-connected fixed-matrix-level finiteness and uniform full-frame scalar identity.
- **step-root-corestriction** [claim](#stmt-full-root-corestriction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-root-corestriction): Regular Hopf socle inclusions and complementary-monomial Koszul chain maps compute transpose root transitions. -> Lower-row vanishing and top oriented corestriction isomorphism.
- **step-perfected-connected-test** [claim](#stmt-full-perfected-connected-calculation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-perfected-connected-calculation): Finite connected corestriction limits followed by uniformly bounded root systems and filtered pro-zero character tests. -> Perfected connected dual calculation and character-vanishing criterion.
- **step-perfected-support-characters** [claim](#stmt-full-perfected-support-characters) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-perfected-support-characters): Compute finite-field support orientation, Honda volume, and top translation characters, then apply the perfected character test. -> Only norm characters on perfected connected cohomology.
- **step-perfected-row-filtration** [claim](#stmt-full-perfected-row-characters) / [proof](#proof-stmt-full-perfected-row-characters): Algebraic matrix-level unions preserve tame norm characters; finite row bounds and the pro-group augmentation filtration refine to norm lines. -> Norm-character filtrations on actual perfected individual rows.
- **step-coefficient-induction** [claim](#stmt-thm-coefficient-finiteness) / [proof](#eq:compact:induction-order): Lexicographic induction proves compact, bounded-pole, and full-frame assertions in order; every cross-pair appeal decreases the stated measure. -> Complete coefficient finiteness theorem with common finite stages.

- **step-modification-transport** [claim](#stmt-prop-modification-transport) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-modification-transport): Finite constant-section maps and arithmetic primary decomposition isolate constants; upper-block inflation identifies the extension-space action. -> Actual multiplicative sphere-cochain transport and block action.
- **step-k-continuity** [claim](#stmt-gen-k-continuity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gen-k-continuity): Bounded coefficient and Postnikov continuity carries finite standard representations through the congruence tower. -> Continuous additive completed K-theory class compatible with blocks.

- **step-top-volume** [claim](#stmt-lem-top-volume) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-top-volume): Transgressed Chern volumes, integral simplex-cocycle valuation, and congruence subgroup indices identify the top lattice. -> Exact integral top cohomology lattice and unit primitive product coefficient.

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-frame-torsor",
          "exact_quote": "The rings $B_U$ form a tower of finite étale $B$-algebras. After passing to normal open levels, the maps in the tower are finite étale torsors for the indicated finite deck groups. The tower is $P_n$-equivariant, and $P_n$ commutes with its $U_0$-action.*\n\n\n\n\n*Over $\\mathcal B$, the scheme of lifts of the compatible étale basis is an affine faithfully flat torsor for $$\\label{rings:translation-group}\n T=(T_p\\Gamma_t)^m,\n \\qquad\n T_p\\Gamma_t=\\varprojlim_{[p]}\\Gamma_t[p^r].$$ For every $r\\geq1$ its finite quotient has group $T/[p]^rT=\\Gamma_t[p^r]^m$ and algebra $$\\label{rings:root-torsor}\n \\mathcal B^{1/p^{tr}}.$$ Thus the full lift algebra is the algebraic root union $\\mathcal B^{\\mathrm{perf}}$. The group $P_n$ acts trivially on the translation parameters. The action of $(h,a)\\in U_0$ on a translation tuple $\\tau$ is $$\\label{rings:auxiliary-action}\n \\tau\\longmapsto h\\tau a^{-1}.$$ All finite torsor constructions and all their morphisms descend to finite frame levels once their finite marking data are included.",

        }

At this level $$\\mathcal O((\\Gamma_t^\\vee[p^r])^m)\n   =\\Lambda_q:=\\Lambda/(D_1^q,\\ldots,D_d^q),\n \\qquad\n \\dim_k\\Lambda_q=q^d=Q^m.$$ The embedding $[p]^r:T\\hookrightarrow T$ corresponds on distributions to $$\\psi_q:\\Lambda\\longrightarrow\\Lambda,\n \\qquad D_j\\longmapsto D_j^q,\\quad c\\longmapsto c\\ (c\\in k).$$ If $N_q=\\mathcal O(T/[p]^rT)$ is the regular function representation, finite Hopf duality gives a normalized equivariant identification $N_q\\simeq\\Lambda_q$ as translation representations.           "exact_quote": "Let $r$ be one of the chosen levels and put $H=[p]^rT$. Transport a finite $T$-representation $M$ to $H$ using $[p]^r:T\\simeq H$, and then coinduce it to $T$. This is an exact functor, denoted $\\mathcal C_r$. There is a natural $P_n$- and auxiliary-equivariant identification of the associated coefficient diagram for $\\mathcal C_rM$ with the $Q$-root version of the diagram for $M$. Powering by $Q$ identifies the two diagrams $k$-linearly and Frobenius-semilinearly over the base: $$\\label{rings:power-scalar-rule}\n \\Phi_Q(cf)=c^Q\\Phi_Q(f),\\qquad \\Phi_Q(f)=f^Q.$$ The assertion holds for every morphism and every finite diagram, and after invariants in any compatible open frame subgroup.           "anchor": "stmt-lem-cartier-transfer",
          "exact_quote": "Fix one sufficiently divisible step with function-root exponent $Q$, and use the volume just constructed. The quotient transfers of the lift torsors can be normalized compatibly so that, after powering to a fixed finite frame ring, their first step is $$\\label{rings:stationary-c}\n S(f)=\\frac{\\mathscr C_Q(f\\eta)}{\\eta},$$ where $\\mathscr C_Q$ is Cartier trace on continuous top differentials. They commute with $P_n$, with their natural auxiliary actions, and with finite étale change of frame level. Before stationary identification it is the inclusion into the next root coefficient ring. For a finite étale cover or its associated coefficient module, this is the actual Frobenius on the cover functions and their trace duals.           "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal G$ be the algebraic height-$s$, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group obtained from the universal formal deformation, and let $\\mathcal R_s$ be its characteristic-$p$ complete local deformation ring. There is a functorial height-one, dimension-one Barsotti–Tate group $$\\mathcal H_{\\det}=\\bigwedge^s\\mathcal G.$$ Its marked deformation is canonically constant. The covariant action of $P_s$ on its special group, and hence on this constant marked deformation, is multiplication by the actual unit $\\operatorname{Nrd}(g)\\in\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$.*\n\n*With the convention that actions on functions use inverse substitution, put $$\\mathcal N_s=\n       \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathcal R_s}(\\omega_{\\mathcal H_{\\det}},\\mathcal R_s).$$ Then there is a $P_s$-equivariant identification $$\\mathcal N_s\\simeq\n                 \\mathcal R_s\\otimes_k k(\\nu_s).$$ Every integral tensor power of this line is admissible on every starting-height quotient of the deformation disc and on its labeled disc. The assertion is preserved by the finite root transports and the successive boundary restrictions used in Definition <a href=\"#def:compact:admissible\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:compact:admissible\">12</a>.",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-ordered-filtration-unit**: The chromatic overlap has an ordered filtration with the specified localized-sphere cofibers, and its first-stage comparison is the canonical localization unit. The attaching maps remain part of the construction.
- **invariant-common-product-family**: A common family of sphere classes supplies the specified product-basis equivalences at every lower positive height; the empty product is the unit.
- **invariant-algebraic-cochain-topology**: A cochain on a compact source uses a common finite coefficient stage and a common pole bound. Forming the algebraic coefficient union preserves this convention.
- **invariant-actual-transfer-transpose**: The normalized torsor transfers use Hopf integration. Their residue transpose is the actual positive Frobenius on coefficient functions, retaining the volume line and compatibility with finite diagrams.
- **invariant-derived-translation-action**: Trivial translation action on cohomology does not justify replacing the action on the coefficient complex by a trivial derived action. The natural top-edge insertion supplies the comparison used after matrix-group cohomology.
- **invariant-independent-rational-block**: Rational homotopy dimensions determine the last filtration block. Its individual generators are chosen separately from the specified positive-height product bases.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-outside-prime-range**: Apply the ordered-filtration theorem outside its stated prime range or treat that range as an established sharp threshold. -> The hypotheses no longer supply the claimed filtration, and the paper does not establish sharpness.
- **anti-use-split-wedge**: Replace the filtration by a wedge of its cofibers or infer a retraction of the unit. -> This discards attaching maps whose vanishing is not established by the filtration.
- **anti-use-rational-products**: Assign the final rational pieces to products involving the last generator. -> The rational dimension calculation does not identify those product maps with the chosen rational basis.
- **anti-use-completed-coefficient-substitution**: Replace the algebraic marking union by an analytic completion or allow coefficient stages and poles to vary without a common bound on a compact source. -> The replacement changes the coefficient complex used by the ordinary residue comparison.
- **anti-use-arbitrary-semilinear-transpose**: Substitute an arbitrary semilinear operator with matching ranks for the geometric transfer transpose. -> Rank agreement does not provide the actual Frobenius on finite-cover functions required by the integral support comparison.
- **anti-use-cohomological-formality**: Infer that the translation action on the complex is trivial merely because it is trivial on cohomology. -> Derived translation extensions can survive the passage to cohomology rows.
- **anti-use-independent-height-generators**: Assemble the filtration from unrelated abstract bases selected separately at each height. -> Removing an earlier quotient block need not remove the corresponding summands in every later height test.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The filtration is a construction in a stable category of spectra, with continuous cochains, completed descent, and rational basis choices; the paper does not provide a finite executable presentation of its maps or attaching data. The assembly proof explicitly states: "The derived category of $\mathbb Q_p$-vector spaces splits by homology." It then states: "Choose a basis in each degree to obtain an equivalence of rational $S$-modules" before the displayed rational-block equivalence. Finite checks of subset indices or degree identities would not certify those spectrum-level constructions or the simultaneous localization equivalences.

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The filtration is constructed in a stable category from specified spectral maps. The paper supplies no executable representation of these maps or procedure for computing their attachments. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The geometric extension locus parametrizes exact sequences of bundles rather than states, update rules, or physical trajectories for a simulation. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The coefficient convention constrains continuous mathematical cochains through common finite stages and bounded poles. It does not specify a tool interface or a finite representation that a symbolic system can manipulate directly. |
| algorithms | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The assembly criterion constructs spectral quotients under equivalence and rational-dimension hypotheses, but provides no effective method for deciding those hypotheses or computing the required maps. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The labeled rings are formal power-series algebras. Their finite freeness over the deformation ring does not provide finite storage for their elements or a concrete data structure for the full tower. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The Cartier transfer is defined through continuous top differentials and finite Hopf integration. The paper gives no bounded arithmetic workload or hardware realization of this operation. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Finite frame torsors and their commuting actions establish geometric descent. They supply neither a cryptographic primitive nor a computational hardness assumption. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The specified exterior-algebra basis describes exact continuous cohomology. It supplies no trainable model, statistical objective, or learning construction. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The filtration order follows subset maxima to remove chromatic layers. The theorem supplies no objective function or optimality assertion for choosing that order. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Uniform equivariance places translation-extension comparisons at a common mathematical frame level. It does not construct a communication protocol, replicated state, or fault-tolerant execution mechanism. |
| other (Chromatic homotopy theory) | True | strong | adaptable | inferred | The paper constructs an ordered filtration of the chromatic overlap by successive cofibers. Its assembly proof removes compatible basis maps in height blocks, chooses the final rational block from dimensions, and recovers the stages by fibers and intermediate pullbacks. This is a concrete mathematical construction suitable for adaptation to a symbolic framework capable of representing the required spectra and maps; an executable realization is ABSENT. |

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-generic-prime-range** (hypothesis): The main ordered-filtration assertion requires the stated positive height and generic prime inequality. It supplies neither a conclusion for excluded primes nor a sharpness theorem. Blocked use: ['Apply the main filtration theorem outside its prime range.', 'Claim that the prime inequality is necessary.']
- **limit-local-module-category** (formal_scope): The filtration and its maps belong to the specified category of localized modules over the completed sphere; the theorem does not give an unrestricted construction for arbitrary spectra. Blocked use: ['Transport the cofiber descriptions to an unspecified scalar category without a comparison theorem.']
- **limit-retained-extensions** (formal_scope): The filtration retains its attaching maps. Its cofiber list does not establish a wedge decomposition or a retraction of the canonical unit. Blocked use: ['Replace the target by a wedge of its cofibers.', 'Declare the unit split solely from the filtration.']
- **limit-common-specified-basis-maps** (hypothesis): Assembly requires the same specified component maps to provide compatible bases at every required positive height. Separate abstract rank calculations do not establish this compatibility. Blocked use: ['Assemble independently chosen local bases with no common underlying maps.', 'Infer the specified product equivalences from matching dimensions alone.']
- **limit-rational-final-block** (formal_scope): The last rational block is selected using rational dimensions. The source leaves its individual pieces unidentified with the specified products containing the final index. Blocked use: ['Assign the rational final-block maps to those products without an additional argument.']
- **limit-height-one-unit** (edge_case): The rational endpoint of the assembly criterion additionally requires a nonzero rationalized unit. The dimension formula alone does not verify that condition. Blocked use: ['Use the endpoint assembly argument with a zero prescribed map.']
- **limit-algebraic-common-stage-topology** (hypothesis): Continuous cochains on compact sources must have a common pole bound and, in coefficient unions, a common finite stage. Analytic completion or unrestricted variation of stages changes the coefficient problem. Blocked use: ['Replace the algebraic frame union by completed analytic functions in the residue test.', 'Allow unbounded denominators on a compact cochain source.']
- **limit-recursive-admissibility** (hypothesis): Compact finiteness applies to admissible coefficients with the required constant-frame filtrations and module splittings on every successive labeled boundary stratum. Finite freeness alone is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Apply compact coefficient finiteness to an arbitrary finite free module with a continuous action.', 'Check admissibility only on the initial exact-height open.']
- **limit-unreduced-full-section-data** (formal_scope): The full-section presentations and boundary descent retain nilpotent test rings and finite torsion-coordinate factors. Reduced geometric-point data do not replace these coefficients. Blocked use: ['Discard the nilpotent transverse deformation in the pole-removal stage.', 'Identify the full-section coefficient using only reduced fibers.']
- **limit-normalized-hopf-transfer** (hypothesis): The transfer is normalized finite Hopf integration with a specific residue transpose. Ordinary field trace or a semilinear matrix having the same ranks cannot replace it in the support comparison. Blocked use: ['Substitute ordinary field trace for torsor integration.', 'Infer the integral norm comparison from rank agreement alone.']
- **limit-distinct-frobenius-exponents** (formal_scope): Function rooting and the Cartier-dual distribution algebra use distinct exponents at the chosen divisible levels. Their roles must remain separate in powering and extension comparisons. Blocked use: ['Use the distribution exponent as the function-root exponent in the positive-lattice estimate.']
- **limit-multiplicative-translation-case** (edge_case): At multiplicative starting height, translations are diagonalizable and invariants are exact. The positive-dimensional power-series distribution argument and higher translation Ext are not used in that case. Blocked use: ['Apply the connected Cartier-dual Koszul argument unchanged at multiplicative height.']
- **limit-buffered-supports-and-almost-comparison** (hypothesis): The support calculations use bounded subdomains with strict radius gaps, and the positive extension comparison is an almost equivalence. These conclusions do not supply arbitrary boundary purity or an ordinary integral isomorphism. Blocked use: ['Discard the support-buffer convention in the analytic comparison.', 'Promote an almost equivalence to an ordinary integral equivalence without further evidence.', 'Assert coherent purity across an arbitrary characteristic boundary.']
- **limit-ordered-coefficient-induction** (hypothesis): The coefficient proof uses earlier height pairs and proves compact, bounded-pole, and full-frame assertions in their specified order. The current full-frame assertion cannot be assumed in its own compact or bounded-pole proof. Blocked use: ['Close the coefficient argument by circularly invoking the current full-frame conclusion.', 'Apply arbitrary stabilizer representation twists in place of the established norm-filtered boundary rows.']
- **limit-root-transition-directions** (formal_scope): Stationary power transport identifies individual coefficient problems but does not identify the actual root inclusions with transfer maps or isomorphisms. The perfected character argument depends on the directions of their transposes. Blocked use: ['Replace root-inclusion transitions by stationary powering isomorphisms.', 'Interchange root inclusion and Hopf transfer when forming limits.']
- **limit-derived-translation-action** (formal_scope): Triviality of translation action on cohomology does not trivialize the action on the complex. The natural top-edge comparison is used with the derived action retained. Blocked use: ['Assume equivariant formality from trivial cohomology-row actions.', 'Replace the derived translation complex by an arbitrary split sum of its rows.']
- **limit-integral-stable-generator-range** (hypothesis): The selected sphere representatives and integral regulator normalizations are established in their stated rank and twist ranges, with specified local coordinate and period conventions. Blocked use: ['Extend sphere-lifting conclusions to higher ranks without checking the comparison range.', 'Change the period basis while preserving the stated integral exponential lattice formula unchanged.']
- **limit-ordinary-residue-of-completed-terms** (hypothesis): The residue comparison applies ordinary smash to the completed descent terms and recovers algebraic connected-marking cochains with their semilinear coface and actual unit action. It does not authorize replacing either side by a different completed coefficient construction. Blocked use: ['Change ordinary residue smash to an unspecified completed tensor operation.', 'Drop source-field factors or the semilinear first coface before descent.']
- **limit-exact-descent-convergence** (hypothesis): The exact-functor totalization result uses the quickly convergent completed Morava descent tower. Strong spectral-sequence convergence with a finite filtration also requires the stated bounded cohomological range. Blocked use: ['Infer that arbitrary exact functors preserve arbitrary infinite totalizations.', 'Infer the finite-filtration conclusion without its bounded-page condition.']
- **limit-noncanonical-rational-basis-choice** (nonconstructive): The rational assembly step chooses homology bases in a rational derived category. The proof does not supply finite executable encodings of the resulting spectral maps or their attachments. Blocked use: ['Treat finite subset enumeration as a certificate for the entire spectral filtration.', 'Advertise a terminating implementation of the assembly criterion from the existence proof alone.']
- **limit-compactness-not-effective-enumeration** (nonconstructive): The compact finiteness argument passes through countability and compactness. It does not enumerate a basis or give a computational cost for the resulting cohomology. Blocked use: ['Interpret cohomological finiteness as an algorithm for listing representatives.', 'Assign an implementation complexity from the compactness proof.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every <i>n</i> ≥ 1 and prime $`p\gt n+1`$, we construct a $`2^n`$-stage ordered filtration of $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge`$ with the classical chromatic-splitting cofibers. The map from the first stage to the target is the canonical localization unit.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

Chromatic localization separates stable homotopy theory into heights. The fracture square relates height $n$ to the lower heights through the overlap $$X_{n,p}=L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge.$$ Here $K(n)$ is Morava $K$-theory, $L_{K(n)}$ is its localization, and $L_r=L_{E(r)}$ is localization at Johnson–Wilson theory; $L_0$ is rationalization. Describing this overlap requires both its pieces and the maps that attach them.

We prove a filtered form of chromatic splitting in the range $p>n+1$. The cofibers are the sphere localizations in the classical strong splitting list, but their extensions are retained. The map from the first stage to $X_{n,p}$ is the canonical localization unit. The proof constructs one family of product maps before applying any lower-height test.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The theorem

Put $S=S_p^\wedge$ and $D=L_{K(n)}S$. For a finite set $I$ of positive integers, write $$d(I)=\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1),\qquad d(\varnothing)=0.$$ All filtrations below are in the category of $E(n-1)$-local $S$-modules; equivalences and localizations are detected on the underlying spectra.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1**. *Let $n\geq1$ and let $p>n+1$ be prime. There exist an enumeration $I_1,\ldots,I_{2^n}$ of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a filtration $F_\bullet$, and a family of classes $y_i\in\pi_{1-2i}D$, $1\leq i\leq n$, with the following properties.*

<a id="eq:pieces"></a>
1.  ***Filtration and unit.** The enumeration has $I_1=\varnothing$ and $\max I_j$ nondecreasing for $j\geq2$. The filtration is $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots
     \longrightarrow F_{2^n}\xrightarrow{\simeq}X_{n,p}$$ with $\operatorname{cofib}(F_{j-1}\to F_j)\simeq C_{I_j}$, where $$\label{eq:pieces}
     \begin{aligned}
     C_\varnothing&=L_{n-1}S,\\
     C_I&=\Sigma^{-d(I)}L_{n-\max I}S
           \quad(I\ne\varnothing).
     \end{aligned}$$ Under $F_1=C_\varnothing$, the composite $F_1\to X_{n,p}$ is the canonical localization unit.*

<a id="eq:height-basis"></a>
2.  ***Simultaneous product bases.** For this one family, set $y_\varnothing=1$ and $y_I=y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_r}$ for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_r\}$. For every $1\leq t<n$, the specified map $$\label{eq:height-basis}
     L_{K(t)}
     \left(\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}}
           \Sigma^{-d(I)}S\xrightarrow{(y_I)}D\right)
     \quad\text{is an equivalence}.$$*

</div>

The product bases are the input to the filtration criterion of Proposition <a href="#prop:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:assembly">2</a>. Its construction removes the pieces in blocks of decreasing chromatic height. For $n>1$, the first block consists of the unit and the degree-$-1$ piece, both localized at $E(n-1)$. For $2\leq j<n$, the block with $\max I=j$ has $2^{j-1}$ pieces; after removing it, the remaining quotient has height at most $n-j-1$. The last quotient is rational, and its $2^{n-1}$ pieces are chosen from rational dimensions. Those last pieces are not identified with the products $y_I$ containing $n$.

The resulting filtration retains the attaching maps. Thus the theorem answers the ordered-filtration formulation studied here; it does not assert the classical wedge decomposition or a retraction of the unit. We make no sharpness claim for the prime bound.

At height one the two cofibers are $H\mathbb Q_p$ and $\Sigma^{-1}H\mathbb Q_p$. At height three, where the range is $p\geq5$, one permitted order is $$\begin{gathered}
 L_2S,\quad\Sigma^{-1}L_2S,\quad
 \Sigma^{-3}L_1S,\quad\Sigma^{-4}L_1S,\\
 \Sigma^{-5}H\mathbb Q_p,\quad\Sigma^{-6}H\mathbb Q_p,\quad
 \Sigma^{-8}H\mathbb Q_p,\quad\Sigma^{-9}H\mathbb Q_p.
\end{gathered}$$

<a id="intro:strategy"></a>
#### Proof strategy

Two issues separate the desired product bases from a calculation of cohomological ranks. The cohomology generators must be represented by sphere classes, and those representatives must induce the required basis under every lower-height test. The proof develops these two inputs separately and compares their actual actions before applying the tests. Figure <a href="#fig:proof-architecture" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:proof-architecture">1</a> shows where they meet.

For the coefficient input, fix $1\leq t<n$, put $m=n-t$, and choose a finite field $k$ containing the Honda fields in use, with degree prime to $p$. The characteristic-$p$ deformation stratum has rings $$A_t=k[[x_t,\ldots,x_{n-1}]],\qquad B_t=A_t[1/x_t].$$ Let $\mathcal B_{n,t}$ be the algebraic union of finite covers of $B_t$ that mark the connected height-$t$ formal group, leaving its étale Tate module unmarked. A cochain on a compact source uses one finite cover and one common pole bound. Write $P_n$ for the ordinary height-$n$ stabilizer, the unit group of the maximal order in the division algebra over $\mathbb Q_p$ of invariant $1/n$.

Sections <a href="#sec:rings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:rings">3</a>–<a href="#sec:support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:support">5</a> compare these algebraic coefficients with integral compact supports. Finite covers that mark both the connected group and its étale basis carry translation torsors. Their normalized transfers have a concrete feature: in invariant-volume coordinates, the transpose is the actual Frobenius on finite-cover functions. The perfected frame quotient is a space of independent bundle extensions. Its compact supports, computed by a rational flag resolution, give a finite stable transfer image.

The passage from that stable image to coefficient finiteness is a three-part induction, organized in Theorem <a href="#thm:coefficient-finiteness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:coefficient-finiteness">13</a>. Section <a href="#sec:compact" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compact">6</a> proves compact finiteness using a fixed translation extension operation. Section <a href="#sec:boundary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:boundary">7</a> removes the pole bound by retaining the nilpotent transverse deformation at each boundary stratum. Section <a href="#full:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:section">8</a> then passes to the full frame tower and proves the individual-row norm-character filtrations needed at later boundary steps. The order on $(n,n-t)$ makes these dependencies inductive: a boundary step uses full-frame rows at larger starting height and compact coefficients at smaller total height. Throughout, the constant $P_n$-cochain action is retained.

The second input is one family of stable constants. Sections <a href="#sec:constants" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:constants">9</a>–<a href="#sec:generators" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:generators">10</a> construct $$u_i\in\pi_{1-2i}C^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;S),\qquad 1\leq i\leq n,$$ where the coefficient sphere has trivial $P_n$-action. A common modification space compares division and matrix constant cochains; on the extension space, it identifies the action with upper-left matrix-block restriction. Integral regulator and top-volume calculations normalize the classes so that their mod-$p$ Hurewicz images have nonzero exterior product. Write $\xi_i\in H^{2i-1}_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;k)$ for these images under $S\to H\mathbb F_p$, followed by scalar extension to $k$.

Section <a href="#full:module-section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:module-section">11</a> brings the two inputs together. A parabolic weight calculation and a natural top-edge map identify the coefficient module with the regular exterior module for the specified classes. Its degree-zero generator is the coefficient unit: Proposition <a href="#prop:constant-module" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:constant-module">69</a> proves $$\bigwedge_k(e_1,\ldots,e_m)
\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;\mathcal B_{n,t}),
\qquad e_i\longmapsto\xi_i\cdot1,\quad |e_i|=2i-1.$$ The same rank-$n$ family supplies this map for every $t$.

Finally, Section <a href="#sec:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:spectral">12</a> applies ordinary residue smash to the completed Morava descent resolution. Flatness and finite algebraic base change recover the coefficient complex above, including its semilinear first coface. The classes $u_i$ map to the classes $y_i$ in $D$; their products give compatible lifts of every basis vector through the totalization tower. Consequently the associated-graded basis is realized by the specified maps in <a href="#eq:height-basis" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:height-basis">[eq:height-basis]</a>. Section <a href="#sec:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:assembly">2</a> proves in advance the final step: successive cofibers lower the height of the quotient, rational independence determines its last block, and finite pullbacks produce the filtration with its prescribed unit.

<figure id="fig:proof-architecture">

<figcaption>The two inputs to the prescribed product bases. The left branch keeps the algebraic coefficient topology and its constant-cochain action; the right constructs the classes that act. Ordinary residue descent recognizes their products, and the independent rational calculation supplies the last filtration block.</figcaption>
</figure>

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### History and the ingredients of the proof

Hopkins’ chromatic splitting conjecture, recorded by Hovey (Hovey 1995, Conjecture 4.2) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Hovey](#ref-Hovey)], proposes classes, factorizations, and a splitting of a canonical cofiber sequence. Its weak consequence asks for a retraction of the canonical unit comparison (Hovey 1995, 2) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Hovey](#ref-Hovey)]. Barthel and Beaudry review a revised strong formulation (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, Conjecture 6.3 and Remark 6.4) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)]. The exterior-indexed summand pattern motivates <a href="#eq:pieces" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:pieces">[eq:pieces]</a>; Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> realizes that pattern as the successive cofibers of an ordered filtration in the stated prime range.

Hovey’s July 1993 account records the height-one case and the height-two case at $p>3$ as known, attributing the latter to Hopkins using Shimomura–Yabe (Hovey 1995, 17–19) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Hovey](#ref-Hovey)]. Goerss–Henn–Mahowald prove the height-two splitting at $p=3$ (Goerss, Henn, and Mahowald 2014, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[GHM2014](#ref-GHM2014)]. At height two and prime two, Beaudry disproved the original strong formula (Beaudry 2017, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Beaudry2017](#ref-Beaudry2017)]. Beaudry–Goerss–Henn’s corrected calculation has additional Moore-spectrum terms and retains a split unit (Beaudry, Goerss, and Henn 2022, Theorem 1.1.6) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[BGH2022](#ref-BGH2022)].

Barthel–Schlank–Stapleton–Weinstein determine the rational homotopy of the $K(n)$-local sphere at every positive height and prime (Barthel et al. 2025, Theorem A) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[BSSW](#ref-BSSW)]. Their result gives <a id="eq:rational-dimensions"></a>$$\label{eq:rational-dimensions}
 \dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}L_0D
  =\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\}.$$ This determines the size of the last, rational block. It does not identify the maps in <a href="#eq:height-basis" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:height-basis">[eq:height-basis]</a>. We do not identify its individual rational generators with our integral $y_i$.

Torii developed common-coefficient comparisons between adjacent Morava theories and the localized descent spectral sequences they induce, including the unit comparison and survival of the reduced-norm class (Torii 2011, Theorems 4.7, 6.2, 7.6, and 8.1) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[ToriiTranschromatic](#ref-ToriiTranschromatic)]. The characteristic-$p$ period domains of Barthel–Mann–Ray–Schlank–Senger–Weinstein–Zhou provide a geometric approach to the coheight-one problem. For $n\geq2$, their Corollary B shows that the map $$L_{K(n-1)}S\ \vee\ \Sigma^{-1}L_{K(n-1)}S
       \longrightarrow L_{K(n-1)}D$$ represented by the unit and the Devinatz–Hopkins class admits a retraction when $(p-1)\nmid(n-1)$. Their Theorem C gives the full equivalence at height two and odd primes (Barthel et al. 2026) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BMR](#ref-BMR)]. Their relative two-tower description also identifies the determinant normalization for positive-height strata (Barthel et al. 2026, Theorems 2.0.1 and 2.6.3) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[BMR](#ref-BMR)].

The coefficient distinction emphasized in (Barthel et al. 2026, sec. 1.5) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BMR](#ref-BMR)] is essential here. At intermediate heights $0<t<n-1$, analytic functions on the punctured stratum form a larger ring than the arithmetic coefficients arising from ordinary chromatic base change. Our height test requires the algebraic union $\mathcal B_{n,t}$ with its common finite-stage and bounded-pole cochains. Sections <a href="#sec:support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:support">5</a>–<a href="#full:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="full:section">8</a> connect its cohomology to integral compact supports through transfer and the boundary induction, while retaining that algebraic coefficient convention.

To connect the finite frame tower to integral compact supports, we pass from torsion coordinates to bundle extensions and track the transfer system. Hopkins and Gross relate the rigid generic Lubin–Tate deformation space to projective geometry through an equivariant period map (Hopkins and Gross 1994, Theorem 1) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[HopkinsGross1994](#ref-HopkinsGross1994)]. The finite torsion-coordinate calculation is closely related to Strauch’s analysis of universal formal modules (Strauch 2010) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[Strauch](#ref-Strauch)]; the exact-height connected markings use the formal-group classification in (Lurie 2010, Lecture 14, Theorem 1) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[LurieFormalGroups](#ref-LurieFormalGroups)]. The passage to bundles uses the Fargues–Fontaine curve (Fargues and Fontaine 2018) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[FarguesFontaine](#ref-FarguesFontaine)], the universal-cover description of Scholze–Weinstein (Scholze and Weinstein 2013) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[ScholzeWeinstein](#ref-ScholzeWeinstein)], the relative slope classification of Fargues–Scholze (Fargues and Scholze 2024) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[FarguesScholze](#ref-FarguesScholze)], and the full faithfulness for positive section sheaves of Anschütz–Le Bras (Anschütz and Le Bras 2025) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[AnschuetzLeBrasFourier](#ref-AnschuetzLeBrasFourier)]. Primitive comparison and open–closed localization for integral coefficients supply the geometric comparisons (Scholze 2013; Pignon-Ywanne 2025) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[ScholzeHodge](#ref-ScholzeHodge), [PignonYwanne](#ref-PignonYwanne)]. The compact-parameter and incidence arguments in Section <a href="#sec:support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:support">5</a> establish the uniformity required to apply these comparisons to the finite marking tower and its transfers.

To obtain one family of acting sphere classes, we compare constant cochains and construct stable representatives with integral product normalization. Dotto–Le Hung compute the required mod-$p$ constant cohomology in the range $a<p-1$ (Dotto and Le Hung 2025) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[DLH](#ref-DLH)]; the integral deduction is included in Section <a href="#sec:constants" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:constants">9</a>. The same section uses the integral Drinfeld-space calculation of Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł (Colmez, Dospinescu, and Nizioł 2021) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[CDN](#ref-CDN)] to compare constant cochains through a common modification space. The construction of stable representatives then uses the continuity theorem of Geisser–Hesselholt (Geisser and Hesselholt 2006) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[GeisserHesselholt](#ref-GeisserHesselholt)], in the modern formulation of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow (Clausen, Mathew, and Morrow 2021) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[CMM](#ref-CMM)], the local cyclotomic-trace comparison of Hesselholt–Madsen (Hesselholt and Madsen 1997) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[HesselholtMadsenWitt](#ref-HesselholtMadsenWitt)], and the chosen coordinates in topological cyclic homology of Blumberg–Mandell (Blumberg and Mandell 2023) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[BlumbergMandellTC](#ref-BlumbergMandellTC)]. The regulator comparison of Huber–Kings (Huber and Kings 2011) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[HuberKings](#ref-HuberKings)] and the suspended-Chern volume calculation of Huber–Soergel (Huber and Soergel 2010) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[HuberSoergel](#ref-HuberSoergel)] supply the rational normalization data. Section <a href="#sec:generators" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:generators">10</a> combines them with local lattice and sphere-lifting arguments to obtain the integral normalization needed for the products to remain generators modulo $p$.

<a id="sec:assembly"></a>
### A criterion for the filtration

We first isolate the passage from compatible local bases to an actual filtration. The construction removes the basis maps in blocks, ordered by the largest index in their subsets. Each block kills the highest remaining chromatic layer of the quotient. After the last positive height has been removed, rational independence determines the remaining block. Taking fibers of the quotient maps then recovers a filtration of the original object. The same maps must serve as bases at every height so that removing an earlier block has this prescribed effect on every later test.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### Localizations and scalar conventions

Fix a prime $p$, and write $S=S_p^\wedge$. We work in the stable category of $S$-modules. Localizations are detected on the underlying spectra. In particular, an $S$-module is $E(r)$-local or $K(t)$-local when its underlying spectrum is so. These localizations inherit their $S$-module structure and adjunction from the monoidal Bousfield localization of spectra. All the fibers and cofibers below are taken in $S$-modules.

We use three familiar consequences of chromatic localization:

1.  If $r\geq t$, the localization unit induces $$L_{K(t)}S \xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;} L_{K(t)}L_rS.$$

2.  If an $E(t)$-local object $Q$ satisfies $L_{K(t)}Q=0$, then $Q$ is $E(t-1)$-local. This is the chromatic fracture square applied to $Q$.

3.  $L_0L_rS=L_0S=H\mathbb Q_p$ for every $r\geq0$. Consequently rational $S$-modules are modules over $H\mathbb Q_p$.

The first statement follows because every $E(r)$-equivalence is a $K(t)$-equivalence. Composing localizations gives the first equality in (iii): rationalization is already an $E(r)$-localization of lower height. To identify its value, let $\mathbb S$ denote the sphere before completion. Its positive stable stems are finite: choose an odd sphere in the stable range and apply Serre’s finiteness theorem (Serre 1951, chap. V, Section 3, Proposition 3) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[Serre1951](#ref-Serre1951)]. The Moore exact sequences for $\mathbb S/p^v$ and the Milnor sequence for their inverse limit then give $$\pi_0S=\mathbb Z_p,\qquad
\pi_iS=(\pi_i\mathbb S)^{\wedge}_p\quad(i>0),\qquad
\pi_iS=0\quad(i<0).$$ Indeed, the finite Moore groups satisfy Mittag–Leffler, and the transition on the torsion kernels in the Moore exact sequences is multiplication by $p$, so their inverse limit is zero. Thus the positive groups displayed above are finite $p$-groups. Rationalizing leaves only $\mathbb Q\otimes\mathbb Z_p=\mathbb Q_p$ in degree zero, proving $L_0S=H\mathbb Q_p$. The standard fracture square and these localization conventions are reviewed in (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, sec. 2) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)].

We will also use that the unit of $L_{K(1)}S$ is nonzero after rationalization. At odd $p$, height-one Morava theory is $E_1\simeq KU_p^\wedge$, with $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ acting through Adams operations. The structured homotopy fixed point spectral sequence $$H_c^s(\mathbb Z_p^\times;\pi_rE_1)
\Longrightarrow \pi_{r-s}L_{K(1)}S$$ is strongly convergent (Devinatz and Hopkins 2004, Theorem 1(iii)–(iv) and pp. 2–3) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[DevinatzHopkins](#ref-DevinatzHopkins)]. The $p$-cohomological dimension of $\mathbb Z_p^\times=\mu_{p-1}\times(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$ is one. Since $\pi_*E_1$ is even and the action on $\pi_0E_1=\mathbb Z_p$ is trivial, total degree zero has only the term $H_c^0(\mathbb Z_p^\times;\pi_0E_1)=\mathbb Z_p$. The augmentation sends the actual sphere unit to $1$ on this edge. Hence $\pi_0L_{K(1)}S\cong\mathbb Z_p$, with the unit corresponding to $1$; its rationalization is nonzero.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### The simultaneous basis criterion

For a finite subset $I$ of the positive integers put $$d(I)=\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1),\qquad d(\varnothing)=0.$$ When we refer to a map representing an element of $\pi_{-d(I)}D$, its source is the free $S$-module $\Sigma^{-d(I)}S$.

<a id="stmt-prop-assembly"></a>
<div id="prop:assembly" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2** (Filtration criterion). *Let $n\geq1$, let $p$ be odd, and let $D$ be an $S$-module with a specified map $u:S\to D$. Suppose that maps $$z_I:\Sigma^{-d(I)}S\longrightarrow D,
\qquad I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\},
\qquad z_\varnothing=u,$$ have the following properties.*

1.  *For each $1\leq t<n$, the map with the specified components <a id="eq:criterion-bases"></a>$$\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}}\Sigma^{-d(I)}S
     \xrightarrow{(z_I)} D
    \label{eq:criterion-bases}$$ is a $K(t)$-equivalence.*

2.  *For every integer $b$, <a id="eq:criterion-rational"></a>$$\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}L_0D
    =\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\}.
    \label{eq:criterion-rational}$$ If $n=1$, assume in addition that $\pi_0L_0u$ is nonzero.*

*Then $X=L_{n-1}D$ has the filtration and unit compatibility of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>(a), with $u$ in place of its unit.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-assembly"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-assembly</summary>

*Proof.* First suppose $n>1$. We construct successive quotients $Q_j$ of $X$, starting with $Q_0=X$. The first block is $$B_1=L_{n-1}S\ \vee\ \Sigma^{-1}L_{n-1}S.$$ Localizing the maps $z_\varnothing,z_{\{1\}}$ gives a map $B_1\to Q_0$. Let $Q_1$ be its cofiber. Applying $L_{K(n-1)}$, hypothesis (a) identifies this map with an equivalence. The cofiber $Q_1$ is therefore $E(n-2)$-local.

Inductively, assume that $2\leq j\leq n-1$ and that $Q_{j-1}$ is $E(n-j)$-local. For every $I$ with $\max I=j$, compose $z_I$ with $D\to X\to Q_{j-1}$. The localization adjunction extends this map uniquely, in the space of such extensions, to $\Sigma^{-d(I)}L_{n-j}S$. We thus obtain <a id="eq:block-quotient"></a>$$B_j=\bigvee_{\max I=j}\Sigma^{-d(I)}L_{n-j}S
 \longrightarrow Q_{j-1}\longrightarrow Q_j,
\label{eq:block-quotient}$$ where the last object is the cofiber.

Here is the compatibility needed to continue the induction. Fix $t=n-j$. Hypothesis (a) gives a specified direct-sum basis of $L_{K(t)}D=L_{K(t)}X$, indexed by the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,j\}$. For each earlier block $\ell<j$, its sphere localization has height at least $t$. Its $K(t)$-localization is therefore the corresponding shift of $L_{K(t)}S$, and its map is the image of the original component $z_I$. Successive cofibers of these components remove exactly the subsets whose maximum is less than $j$, together with the empty subset. This assertion is inductive: at each step the map into the cofiber is the composite of that same original component with the quotient map, so the cofiber is the quotient by that direct summand.

The remaining summands are precisely the components of $B_j$. It follows that $L_{K(t)}(B_j\to Q_{j-1})$ is an equivalence. Consequently $L_{K(t)}Q_j=0$, and chromatic fracture makes $Q_j$ $E(t-1)$-local. The construction thus reaches a rational object $Q_{n-1}$. For $n=2$, this is already the object $Q_1$ constructed from the first block.

We next determine that rational quotient, keeping track of possible kernels. The elements $$z_I,\qquad I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\},$$ are linearly independent after rationalization in each degree. Indeed, under hypothesis (a) at $t=1$, their images in $L_{K(1)}D$ are the units of distinct shifted summands $\Sigma^{-d(I)}L_{K(1)}S$. The rationalized unit in each such summand is nonzero. A rational relation between the $z_I$ would therefore give a relation between nonzero elements in different summands, which is impossible. This argument includes subsets with equal values of $d(I)$.

Since $L_0L_rS=H\mathbb Q_p$, rationalizing the map from each block gives, in every degree, the injection of the corresponding independent vectors into the quotient by the preceding vectors. The cofiber long exact sequence has no suspended kernel. Subtracting these vectors from the dimensions in hypothesis (b) leaves $$\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}Q_{n-1}
=\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:\max I=n,\ d(I)=b\}.$$ The derived category of $\mathbb Q_p$-vector spaces splits by homology. Choose a basis in each degree to obtain an equivalence of rational $S$-modules $$B_n=\bigvee_{\max I=n}\Sigma^{-d(I)}H\mathbb Q_p
 \xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;}Q_{n-1}.$$ Its cofiber $Q_n$ is zero.

<a id="eq:filtration-pullback"></a>
It remains to pass from these successive quotients to a filtration of $X$. Set $$G_j=\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(X\longrightarrow Q_j),\qquad 0\leq j\leq n.$$ Then $G_0=0$ and $G_n=X$. For each block the square $$\begin{tikzcd}
G_j \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & B_j \arrow[d]\\
X \arrow[r] & Q_{j-1}
\end{tikzcd}
\label{eq:filtration-pullback}$$ is cartesian: its upper left corner is the fiber of $X\to Q_j=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(B_j\to Q_{j-1})$. Taking fibers of its horizontal maps yields the cofiber sequence $$G_{j-1}\longrightarrow G_j\longrightarrow B_j.$$ If a block is $B_j=C_1\vee\cdots\vee C_r$, replace $G_j$ by the intermediate pullbacks along $$0\longrightarrow C_1\longrightarrow C_1\vee C_2
\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_j.$$ Exactness of pullback in a stable category makes their successive cofibers $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. In the first block choose the unit summand first. Its pullback identifies the first stage with $L_{n-1}S$, and its map to $X$ is exactly the localized $u$. The other blocks are already ordered by maximum. The number of individual pieces is $$2+\sum_{j=2}^{n-1}2^{j-1}+2^{n-1}=2^n.$$ This constructs the required filtration by $S$-linear maps.

If $n=1$, the object $X=L_0D$ is rational. Hypothesis (b) places one copy of $\mathbb Q_p$ in degree zero and one in degree $-1$. The nonzero map $L_0u:H\mathbb Q_p\to X$ is an isomorphism on degree-zero homotopy, so its cofiber is $\Sigma^{-1}H\mathbb Q_p$. These are the two required stages. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-rem-assembly-extensions"></a>
<div id="rem:assembly-extensions" class="remark">

*Remark 3*. The construction uses maps into the current quotient. Diagram <a href="#eq:filtration-pullback" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:filtration-pullback">[eq:filtration-pullback]</a> retains their boundary maps when the blocks are pulled back to $X$. Thus the criterion produces the attaching maps as part of the filtration; it requires no choice of a nullhomotopy for them.

</div>

<a id="sec:rings"></a>
### Finite frame rings and Cartier transfers

To compare coefficient cohomology with compact supports, we need transfers whose transpose is the actual Frobenius on functions of the finite covers. This section constructs the finite frame rings and lift torsors, then normalizes their Cartier transfers to obtain that map in Lemma <a href="#lem:cartier-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cartier-transfer">11</a>.

Fix integers $1\leq t<n<p-1$, and put $m=n-t$. Choose a finite field $k$ containing the fields of definition of the Honda endomorphisms at the heights at most $n$. Its degree over $\mathbb F_p$ may be chosen prime to $p$: a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$ suffices for these endomorphism fields. Further finite extensions used below are chosen with the same property. Write $$A=k[[x_t,\ldots,x_{n-1}]],\qquad x=x_t,\qquad B=A[1/x].$$ Here $A$ is the height-$t$ quotient of the characteristic-$p$ Lubin–Tate deformation ring of the height-$n$ Honda group. Write $\mathcal G_A$ for its formal group and $P_n=\mathcal O_{D_n}^{\times}$ for the ordinary height-$n$ stabilizer. The action on a function induced by a left action on points is always inverse substitution.

<a id="rings:height-congruences"></a>
We choose a coordinate on $\mathcal G_A$ lifting the fixed Honda coordinate and having the height congruences $$\label{rings:height-congruences}
 [p](T)\equiv x_iT^{p^i}
 \pmod{(x_t,\ldots,x_{i-1},T^{p^i+1})},
 \qquad t\leq i\leq n,
 \quad x_n=1.$$ The same choice gives the full special-fiber identity $$[p](T)\equiv T^{p^n}\pmod{(x_t,\ldots,x_{n-1})}$$ as an identity of formal series. Moreover $[p](T)$ factors through $T^{p^t}$ over $A$. The group used on $B$ is the algebraic $p$-divisible group obtained from the finite kernels over $A$. More explicitly, Weierstrass preparation makes $$A[[T]]/([p^l](T))$$ a finite free $A$-algebra of rank $p^{nl}$. Its torsion coordinate is topologically nilpotent before localization, so the formal addition and multiplication series define algebraic group operations on this finite algebra. Preparation for $[p](T)-Z$ gives the finite flat transition maps. We localize these finite group schemes at $x$. Thus the connected–étale sequence on $B$ retains the entire finite kernel, including its infinitesimal connected part.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
#### Labeled rings before localization

For $l\geq1$, consider $m$ points of $\mathcal G_A[p^l]$ whose images form a basis of the étale quotient at the generic point of $A$. Let $\widetilde C_l$ be the reduced closure of this generic lifted-basis locus in the finite scheme of $m$ torsion points, and write $z_{1,l},\ldots,z_{m,l}$ for the lifted coordinates. Set $$w_{i,l}=z_{i,l}^{p^{tl}},\qquad
 C_l=A[w_{1,l},\ldots,w_{m,l}]\subseteq\widetilde C_l.$$ These finite $A$-algebras are complete. A reduced closure is used only to establish their coordinates; the proposition also identifies the unreduced scheme that will be used for descent. For the boundary convention $t=n$, the empty labeled ring is $k$.

<a id="stmt-prop-finite-rings"></a>
<div id="prop:finite-rings" class="proposition">

<a id="rings:regular-coordinates"></a>
**Proposition 4** (Finite labeled rings). *There are compatible identifications $$\label{rings:regular-coordinates}
 C_l=k[[w_{1,l},\ldots,w_{m,l}]],\qquad
 \widetilde C_l=k[[z_{1,l},\ldots,z_{m,l}]],\qquad
 w_{i,l}=z_{i,l}^{p^{tl}}.$$ Both rings are finite free over $A$. On the exact-height locus, $C_l[1/x]$ is the finite étale algebra of bases of the étale $p^l$-torsion. Over this algebra the scheme of all lifts of its universal basis to $\mathcal G_A[p^l]$ has algebra $$\widetilde C_l[1/x]=(C_l[1/x])^{1/p^{tl}},$$ finite locally free of rank $p^{tlm}$.*

<a id="rings:transition-powers"></a>
*The transition maps are finite and injective, and for $j\leq l$ $$\label{rings:transition-powers}
 z_{i,j}\in
 k[[z_{1,l}^{p^{t(l-j)}},\ldots,z_{m,l}^{p^{t(l-j)}}]].$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-finite-rings"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-finite-rings</summary>

*Proof.* The algebra $\widetilde C_l$ is finite and reduced, and each of its irreducible components dominates $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A$ by its definition as a generic closure. It has dimension $m$. Above the closed point of $A$ all torsion coordinates are nilpotent, so there is a unique closed point and its residue field is $k$. Its maximal ideal is generated by the height parameters and the $z_{i,l}$.

<a id="rings:basis-polynomial"></a>
Put $a_i=[p^{l-1}](z_{i,l})$, and for $v\in\mathbb F_p^m$ let $a_v$ be the corresponding formal-group linear combination of the $a_i$. If $W_p(T)$ is the distinguished polynomial for $[p](T)$, then $$\label{rings:basis-polynomial}
 W_p(T)=\prod_{v\in\mathbb F_p^m}(T-a_v)^{p^t}
       =\prod_{v\in\mathbb F_p^m}(T^{p^t}-a_v^{p^t}).$$ Indeed this is the factorization over every geometric generic field: the distinct étale points are indexed by the labels and each has connected multiplicity $p^t$. Both sides are monic of degree $p^n$, so generic density in the reduced algebra proves the identity there.

There is a series $h_l$ with $[p^{l-1}](T)=h_l(T^{p^{t(l-1)}})$. Consequently $a_i^{p^t}$ is a power series in $w_{i,l}$ with coefficients in $A$ and zero constant term. Taking formal-group linear combinations gives the same assertion for every $a_v^{p^t}$. Thus <a href="#rings:basis-polynomial" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:basis-polynomial">[rings:basis-polynomial]</a> is an identity over $C_l$, and modulo $(w_{1,l},\ldots,w_{m,l})$ it becomes $T^{p^n}$. The preparation unit for $[p](T)$ is defined over $A$. All coefficients of $[p](T)$ of degree below $p^n$ therefore vanish in this quotient, and <a href="#rings:height-congruences" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:height-congruences">[rings:height-congruences]</a> successively gives $$x_t=x_{t+1}=\cdots=x_{n-1}=0.$$ The maximal ideal of $C_l$ is generated by its $m$ displayed $w$-coordinates. Since $C_l$ is integral over $A$, its dimension is $m$. It is a regular local ring, and the surjection from $k[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$ taking $W_i$ to $w_{i,l}$ is an isomorphism: a nonzero kernel would lower the dimension of this power-series domain. The identical maximal-ideal argument with the $z_{i,l}$ gives the second identification in <a href="#rings:regular-coordinates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:regular-coordinates">[rings:regular-coordinates]</a>, including the stated inclusion. These finite regular rings are Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $m$; the parameters of $A$ form systems of parameters on them. Their Koszul complexes are exact in positive degree, so the finite modules are flat, hence free, over the local ring $A$.

We next check the finite schemes after localization. Write $$[p^l](T)=g_l(T^{p^{tl}}),\qquad
 g_l(S)=U_l(S)V_l(S),$$ where $U_l$ is a unit and $V_l$ is distinguished of degree $p^{ml}$. The linear coefficient of $g_l$ is a unit times $x^{1+p^t+\cdots+p^{t(l-1)}}$. The invariant-differential identity for this Frobenius-divided homomorphism expresses $g_l'(S)$ as that coefficient times a quotient of unit series. Evaluating in the prepared finite algebra shows that $V_l'$ is a unit after $x$ is inverted. Thus the Frobenius-divided finite group is étale there, of rank $p^{ml}$. Its kernel quotient has removed exactly the connected kernel of rank $p^{tl}$.

The scheme of bases of this étale group is finite étale over $B$. The universal labeled points give a surjection from its algebra to $C_l[1/x]$. It is an isomorphism generically, since the generic closure included every basis. Its kernel is zero: the source is flat over the domain $B$, whereas a kernel vanishing generically would be $B$-torsion. This identifies the basis algebra.

Over this basis algebra, the scheme of lifts of the $m$ basis vectors is a product of torsors for the connected finite kernel. It is finite locally free of rank $p^{tlm}$. Its algebra surjects onto $\widetilde C_l[1/x]$, which is generated by the same lifted coordinates. The latter is free over $C_l[1/x]$ with basis $$\prod_{i=1}^m z_{i,l}^{e_i},\qquad 0\leq e_i<p^{tl}.$$ The two ranks are equal, so the surjection is an isomorphism. This is the assertion about the full lift scheme, rather than its reduction.

A basis at level $j$ lifts to a basis at level $l$ over an extension of every geometric generic field. Hence the transition maps on the reduced closures are injective. They are finite because both rings are finite over $A$. Since $z_{i,j}=[p^{l-j}](z_{i,l})$, factorization through Frobenius and <a href="#rings:regular-coordinates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:regular-coordinates">[rings:regular-coordinates]</a> give <a href="#rings:transition-powers" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:transition-powers">[rings:transition-powers]</a>. ◻

</details>

The underlying regular-quotient and étale-coordinate construction is also described at arbitrary height in (Strauch 2010, secs. 3–4, Proposition 4.1) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[Strauch](#ref-Strauch)]. The explicit rank comparison above records the additional finite-flat statement needed for our translation torsors.

The boundary calculation also needs a presentation that survives nilpotent base change. We establish that presentation before identifying the locus on which a label vanishes.

<a id="stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation"></a>
<div id="rings:full-sections-presentation" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5** (An integral full-section presentation). *Let $H$ be the quotient of $\mathcal G_A[p]$ by its relative $p^t$-Frobenius kernel. The ring $C_1$ represents full labeled section tuples $\mathbb F_p^m\to H$, including over nilpotent test rings. Here “full” means equality of the finite Cartier divisors, or equivalently, after every base change, equality of the norm of every function with its product over the labeled sections.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation"><summary>Proof of stmt-rings-full-sections-presentation</summary>

*Proof.* The quotient $H$ has the monogenic presentation obtained by dividing the prepared $p$-series by relative Frobenius. The full-section condition is a finite set of coefficient identities for its monic polynomial. Indeed equality for the coordinate implies equality of the characteristic polynomial for every polynomial in that coordinate by substitution, and every function in the finite algebra has such a representative. This description commutes with arbitrary base change.

Let $Q$ be the resulting finite complete $A$-algebra of labeled group-homomorphism tuples. It has one closed point, because at the closed point of $A$ the connected finite group has only the zero section over a field. If all $m$ labeled coordinates are set equal to zero, the full-section identity makes the divided distinguished polynomial $T^{p^m}$. Applying <a href="#rings:height-congruences" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:height-congruences">[rings:height-congruences]</a> before this division successively kills all the height parameters. Thus the maximal ideal of $Q$ has at most $m$ generators. There is a surjection $Q\twoheadrightarrow C_1$ induced by the generic full tuple. Since $C_1$ has dimension $m$, the dimension and embedding dimension of $Q$ are both $m$. Hence $Q$ is regular. A quotient of this regular local domain of the same dimension has zero kernel, proving $Q=C_1$.

All equations in this argument are equations in finite algebras formed before localization. Their subsequent use on an étale component therefore involves polynomial operations in a finite algebra; it does not require substituting an order-one element into an unevaluated formal series. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-rings-boundary-labels"></a>
<div id="rings:boundary-labels" class="corollary">

<a id="rings:height-divisor"></a>
**Corollary 6** (Vanishing labels and higher starting height). *At level one, for each nonzero label $v\in\mathbb F_p^m$ there is a coordinate $w_v$ such that $$\label{rings:height-divisor}
 x=\text{a unit}\cdot\prod_{0\ne v\in\mathbb F_p^m}w_v.$$ Each ideal $(w_v)$ is $P_n$-stable. Its conormal is a power of the invariant coordinate line. For a primitive label, the quotient by $(w_v)$ is the starting-height-$(t+1)$ level-one ring with $p$-th roots of its parameters adjoined. The same assertion can be iterated for any independent set of dead labels.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-rings-boundary-labels"><summary>Proof of stmt-rings-boundary-labels</summary>

*Proof.* At level one let $a_v$ be the formal-group linear combination of $z_{1,1},\ldots,z_{m,1}$ with label $v\in\mathbb F_p^m$, and put $w_v=a_v^{p^t}$. The coefficient of $T^{p^t}$ in <a href="#rings:basis-polynomial" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:basis-polynomial">[rings:basis-polynomial]</a>, together with the preparation unit, gives <a href="#rings:height-divisor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:height-divisor">[rings:height-divisor]</a>. Transport by $P_n$ is a change of formal coordinate with invertible linear coefficient. Its action on $w_v$ is $w_v$ times a unit, proving stability of $(w_v)$. On the conormal only that linear coefficient remains, raised to the $p^t$-th power. Equivalently, this is the invariant cotangent line of the Frobenius-divided group restricted to its zero section. This also describes the action without a choice of generator for the line.

Change the labels so that $v$ is the first basis vector, and put $R=C_1/(w_1)=k[[w_2,\ldots,w_m]]$. Write $[p](T)=g_t(T^{p^t})$ and let $Q_t$ be the distinguished polynomial of $g_t$. Formula <a href="#rings:height-divisor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rings:height-divisor">[rings:height-divisor]</a> gives $x_t=0$ in $R$. The labels in each coset of $\mathbb F_pv$ then give the same point, so $$Q_t(Y)=\prod_{\bar v\in\mathbb F_p^{m-1}}
              (Y^p-w_{\bar v}^{p}).$$ Over $A/(x_t)$ we have $g_t(Y)=g_{t+1}(Y^p)$, and uniqueness of preparation gives $Q_t(Y)=Q_{t+1}(Y^p)$. Therefore $$Q_{t+1}(Z)=\prod_{\bar v\in\mathbb F_p^{m-1}}(Z-w_{\bar v}^p).$$ Coefficient Frobenius identifies these labels with the formal-group combinations of $w_2^p,\ldots,w_m^p$ in the next Frobenius twist. By Lemma <a href="#rings:full-sections-presentation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rings:full-sections-presentation">5</a>, the displayed full-section identity gives a map from the starting-height-$(t+1)$ labeled ring, whose labeled coordinates map to $w_2^p,\ldots,w_m^p$. In the power-series coordinates of Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-rings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-rings">4</a>, this map is injective with image $k[[w_2^p,\ldots,w_m^p]]=R^p$, since $k$ is perfect. Thus $R$ is exactly its $p$-th-root extension, with the indicated $A/(x_t)$-structure. Repeating the calculation for $h$ independent dead labels sends the higher-height labeled coordinates to $w_{h+i}^{p^h}$ and gives the corresponding $p^h$-th-root extension. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
#### Connected markings and compatible lifts

Let $\Gamma_t$ be the height-$t$ Honda group over $k$. A connected marking is an isomorphism $$\alpha:\Gamma_t\longrightarrow \mathcal G_B^0$$ of formal groups, and an étale marking is an integral basis $i:\mathbb Z_p^m\longrightarrow T_p\mathcal G_B^{\mathrm{et}}$. Their joint algebraic tower has structure group $$U_0=P_t\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_m(\mathbb Z_p),\qquad
 P_t=\mathcal O_{D_t}^{\times}.$$ We use the left action $(h,a)(\alpha,i)=(\alpha h^{-1},ia^{-1})$. For an open subgroup $U\subseteq U_0$, write $B_U$ for the corresponding finite frame algebra. Write $\mathcal B=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U B_U$ for the entire joint algebraic frame ring. No completion of this union is part of this notation.

<a id="stmt-prop-frame-torsor"></a>
<div id="prop:frame-torsor" class="proposition">

**Proposition 7** (Frame and lift torsors). *The rings $B_U$ form a tower of finite étale $B$-algebras. After passing to normal open levels, the maps in the tower are finite étale torsors for the indicated finite deck groups. The tower is $P_n$-equivariant, and $P_n$ commutes with its $U_0$-action.*

<a id="rings:translation-group"></a>
<a id="rings:root-torsor"></a>
<a id="rings:auxiliary-action"></a>
*Over $\mathcal B$, the scheme of lifts of the compatible étale basis is an affine faithfully flat torsor for $$\label{rings:translation-group}
 T=(T_p\Gamma_t)^m,
 \qquad
 T_p\Gamma_t=\varprojlim_{[p]}\Gamma_t[p^r].$$ For every $r\geq1$ its finite quotient has group $T/[p]^rT=\Gamma_t[p^r]^m$ and algebra $$\label{rings:root-torsor}
 \mathcal B^{1/p^{tr}}.$$ Thus the full lift algebra is the algebraic root union $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{perf}}$. The group $P_n$ acts trivially on the translation parameters. The action of $(h,a)\in U_0$ on a translation tuple $\tau$ is $$\label{rings:auxiliary-action}
 \tau\longmapsto h\tau a^{-1}.$$ All finite torsor constructions and all their morphisms descend to finite frame levels once their finite marking data are included.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-frame-torsor"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-frame-torsor</summary>

*Proof.* Over $B$ the lower height coefficients vanish and the height-$t$ coefficient is invertible. The full isomorphism ring between this law and $\Gamma_t$ is therefore a filtered union of finite étale extensions, by the exact-height isomorphism theorem (Lurie 2010, Lecture 14, Theorem 1) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[LurieFormalGroups](#ref-LurieFormalGroups)]. For clarity, its finite stages record coefficients of a full isomorphism that extend to the next required equations. The first coefficient $c$ satisfies $c^{p^t-1}=x^{-1}$ up to the chosen leading unit. The subsequent free coefficients satisfy monic additive equations with invertible linear coefficient; the other coefficients are uniquely determined. The equation constraining a coefficient of degree $p^j$ can occur at degree $p^{t+j}$. Thus these are not the schemes of arbitrary finite-bud isomorphisms. Any two full markings differ uniquely by $P_t$, and quotienting by an open subgroup gives its finite étale torsor stages.

The étale Tate basis tower is finite étale at each level, as proved in Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-rings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-rings">4</a>. Taking the product of the two frame torsors proves the first assertion. Universal deformation transport carries both markings along the same isomorphism; it commutes with changing the markings. This proves the asserted $P_n$ equivariance.

At finite level $r$, two lifts of the marked étale basis differ by exactly one element of $\Gamma_t[p^r]^m$.
