Taking invariants of an isolated factor would not make sense, since that factor is not $\Gamma$-stable. The test periodicity is fixed throughout, so $\kappa_{t,r}$ is an untwisted coefficient line. This gives <a href="#spec:residue-complex" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="spec:residue-complex">[spec:residue-complex]</a>, naturally for constants and their products. ◻

</details>

The use of ordinary smash here also respects the scalar convention of the theorem. The cofiber of $S_{(p)}\to S_p^\wedge$ is rational: it is $p$-local and multiplication by $p$ on it is an equivalence, since the map is an equivalence modulo $p$. Its smash with $\kappa_t$ is zero. Consequently $\kappa_t\wedge S\simeq\kappa_t$, and for an $S$-module $M$, ordinary residue smash agrees with the corresponding relative $S$-module test. All the maps used below are thus maps of $S$-modules.

<a id="pm-h-63"></a>
#### The specified bases survive

<a id="stmt-thm-height-bases"></a>
<div id="thm:height-bases" class="theorem">

<a id="spec:height-basis"></a>
**Theorem 74** (Simultaneous height bases). *The common classes of Proposition <a href="#spec:global-classes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="spec:global-classes">71</a> satisfy, for every $1\leq t<n$, $$L_{K(t)}\left(
\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-t\}}
 \Sigma^{-d(I)}S\xrightarrow{(y_I)}D
\right)
\quad\text{is an equivalence},
\label{spec:height-basis}$$ where $d(I)=\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1)$, and the empty component is the unit.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-height-bases"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-height-bases</summary>

<a id="spec:test-spectral-sequence"></a>
*Proof.* Use Proposition <a href="#spec:exact-descent" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="spec:exact-descent">70</a> with the exact functor $\kappa_t\wedge-$. Lemma <a href="#lem:ordinary-residue" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ordinary-residue">73</a> identifies the totalization spectral sequence as $$E_2^{s,r}=\kappa_{t,r}\otimes_k
 H^s_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n;\mathcal B_{n,t})
\Longrightarrow\pi_{r-s}(\kappa_t\wedge D).
\label{spec:test-spectral-sequence}$$ By Proposition <a href="#prop:constant-module" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:constant-module">69</a>, this page is free over $\kappa_{t,*}$ with basis $\xi_I\cdot1$, for $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $m=n-t$. These are the images of the reductions of the transported integral classes $\alpha^P_{n,I}$. The basis vector indexed by $I$ lies in bidegree $(s,r)=(d(I),0)$. In particular, the page is zero for $s<0$ or $s>m^2$. This statement uses the constant cup action and the nonzero image of $1$ in that proposition.

We now identify the actual representative of each basis vector. There are two filtrations to distinguish: the source tower of constant sphere cochains is built from connective spectra, whereas the residue tower computing $\kappa_t\wedge D$ is periodic. We first locate a representative in the source filtration and then transport it to the residue filtration.

The empty subset is represented by the unit itself. For a nonempty subset put $b=d(I)>0$. The sphere-cochain representative of $y_I$ has filtration at least $b$. Indeed, the $(b-1)$-st partial totalization of the connective sphere-cochain diagram is $(1-b)$-connective and hence has zero homotopy in degree $-b$. The representative therefore lifts to the fiber of the map to that partial totalization. Its component in filtration $b$, modulo the cochain boundary, is its integral Hurewicz class, whose restriction to $P_n$ is $\alpha^P_{n,I}$. The map <a href="#spec:constant-map" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="spec:constant-map">[spec:constant-map]</a> sends this chosen lift to the completed descent tower. Ordinary residue smash is exact and preserves the partial totalizations and their fibers, so it transports the lift to the residue tower as well. Lemma <a href="#lem:ordinary-residue" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ordinary-residue">73</a> identifies its leading component in <a href="#spec:test-spectral-sequence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="spec:test-spectral-sequence">[spec:test-spectral-sequence]</a> with precisely the specified image of $\alpha^P_{n,I}$. Connectivity was needed only in the source tower.

These representatives come from the source totalization and hence supply compatible lifts through every subsequent partial totalization. Their leading terms cannot support an outgoing differential. Products give the representatives for all subsets. For a coefficient in $\kappa_{t,*}$, choose a lift in $\pi_*E_t$. Its natural action on the residue tower carries these compatible lifts to representatives of the corresponding multiple of each basis vector. Therefore every element of the $E_2$-page has such a lift, so $d_2=0$. Inductively, if the earlier differentials vanish, the same representatives span the next page and force its outgoing differential to vanish. This proves that all differentials vanish; in particular none of the specified vectors can be lost as an incoming boundary.

Strong convergence and the bound $0\leq s\leq m^2$ now give a finite filtration on $\pi_*(\kappa_t\wedge D)$. The actual images of the $y_I$ lift its specified associated-graded basis. The coefficient action preserves every filtration step, so this is a filtration by graded $\kappa_{t,*}$-submodules. Finite filtered linear algebra over the graded field $\kappa_{t,*}$ shows that these images themselves form a basis: independence and spanning follow successively from their lowest nonzero filtration components. It follows that the actual map $$\bigvee_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}
 \Sigma^{-d(I)}\kappa_t
\longrightarrow\kappa_t\wedge D$$ is an equivalence. Since $\kappa_t$ detects $K(t)$-equivalences and ordinary residue smash agrees with the relative scalar test, this proves <a href="#spec:height-basis" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="spec:height-basis">[spec:height-basis]</a> with all its stated components. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-64"></a>
#### Rational dimensions and completion of the proof

The last block of the filtration is rational. We use the following independent calculation of the rational local sphere.

<a id="stmt-thm-rational-sphere"></a>
<div id="thm:rational-sphere" class="theorem">

**Theorem 75** (Barthel–Schlank–Stapleton–Weinstein). *For every prime $p$ and height $n\geq1$, the rational homotopy of the $K(n)$-local sphere is the exterior $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra $$\pi_*L_{K(n)}S\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q
\cong\bigwedge_{\mathbb Q_p}(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_n),
\qquad |\zeta_i|=1-2i,$$ with its natural scalar action induced by the unit. In particular, <a id="spec:rational-dimensions"></a>$$\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}\pi_{-b}L_0D
 =\#\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:d(I)=b\}
\qquad(b\in\mathbb Z).
\label{spec:rational-dimensions}$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-rational-sphere"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-rational-sphere</summary>

*Proof.* This is (Barthel et al. 2025, Theorem A) <a id="pm-cite-140"></a>[[BSSW](#ref-BSSW)], with the generator degrees displayed in homotopical grading. Replacing the sphere by its $p$-completion does not change its positive-height localization. The dimension formula is the monomial basis of the exterior algebra. Only this additive formula and the natural scalar action are needed below; no identification of the individual $\zeta_i$ with the classes $y_i$ is required. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-rational-sphere-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-rational-sphere</summary>

*Proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.* Proposition <a href="#spec:global-classes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="spec:global-classes">71</a> supplies the one family $y_i$, its ordered products, and $y_\varnothing=1$. For $n>1$, take $z_I=y_I$, for $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, and take the specified map $u=y_\varnothing:S\to D$ to be the unit. Theorem <a href="#thm:height-bases" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:height-bases">74</a> verifies all the simultaneous local basis hypotheses of Proposition <a href="#prop:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:assembly">2</a>; Theorem <a href="#thm:rational-sphere" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:rational-sphere">75</a> verifies its rational dimension hypothesis. That proposition constructs the successive quotient blocks and pulls them back to a filtration of $L_{n-1}D$, with the required individual cofibers. Under the first-stage identification $F_1=L_{n-1}S$, the composite $F_1\to L_{n-1}D=X_{n,p}$ is the localized unit. All maps and cofibers are $S$-linear, as required.

When $n=1$, Proposition <a href="#spec:global-classes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="spec:global-classes">71</a> still supplies $y_1$; only the positive-height tests are vacuous. The unit calculation in Section <a href="#sec:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:assembly">2</a> and the dimensions of Theorem <a href="#thm:rational-sphere" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:rational-sphere">75</a> verify the remaining hypotheses of Proposition <a href="#prop:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:assembly">2</a>. Its height-one case gives the two cofibers $H\mathbb Q_p$ and $\Sigma^{-1}H\mathbb Q_p$, with the composite from the first stage to $X_{1,p}$ equal to the canonical localization unit. ◻

</details>

      "caption": "The two inputs to the prescribed product bases. The left branch keeps the algebraic coefficient topology and its constant-cochain action; the right constructs the classes that act.       "pdf_page": 5,
      "source_evidence": [

          "anchor": "fig:proof-architecture",
          "exact_quote": "The two inputs to the prescribed product bases. The left\nbranch keeps the algebraic coefficient topology and its constant-cochain\naction; the right constructs the classes that act. Ordinary residue\ndescent recognizes their products, and the",
          "source_object": "fig:0001"
        }
      ],
      "source_kind": "tikz_pgf",
      "tikz_pgf_source": "\\begin{tikzpicture}[\n  every node/.style={align=center,font=\\small},\n  box/.style={draw,rounded corners=2pt,inner sep=6pt,text width=5.9cm}\n]\n\\node[box] (geometry) at (-3.25,0)\n  {Finite frames, transfers, and compact supports\\\\\n   Sections~\\ref{sec:rings}--\\ref{sec:support}};\n\\node[box,anchor=north] (finiteness)\n  at ([yshift=-7mm]geometry.south)\n  {Coefficient finiteness and full-frame rows\\\\\n   Sections~\\ref{sec:compact}--\\ref{full:section}};\n\\node[box] (classes) at (3.25,-1.1)\n  {One integral sphere-cochain family\\\\\n   Sections~\\ref{sec:constants}--\\ref{sec:generators}};\n\\node[box,text width=9cm,anchor=north] (module)\n  at ([xshift=3.25cm,yshift=-8mm]finiteness.south)\n  {The coefficient unit generates\\\\the specified exterior module\\\\\n   Proposition~\\ref{prop:constant-module}};\n\\node[box,text width=9cm,anchor=north] (bases)\n  at ([yshift=-7mm]module.south)\n  {The specified products form a basis\\\\at every lower positive height\\\\\n   Theorem~\\ref{thm:height-bases}};\n\\node[box,text width=9cm,anchor=north] (filtration)\n  at ([yshift=-7mm]bases.south)\n  {Fracture and rational dimensions\\\\give the ordered filtration\\\\\n   Proposition~\\ref{prop:assembly}};\n\\draw[->] (geometry) -- (finiteness);\n\\draw[->] (finiteness) -- (module);\n\\draw[->] (classes) -- (module);\n\\draw[->] (module) -- (bases);\n\\draw[->] (bases) -- (filtration);\n\\end{tikzpicture}",
      "witness_description": "Flowchart diagram showing the structure of the proof with six rectangular nodes and directed connecting edges:\n- Top-left node: \"Finite frames, transfers,\\nand compact supports\\nSections 3–5\"\n- Node below top-left: \"Coefficient finiteness\\nand full-frame rows\\nSections 6–8\"\n- Top-right node: \"One integral sphere-cochain family\\nSections 9–10\"\n- Middle centered node: \"The coefficient unit generates\\nthe specified exterior module\\nProposition 11.4\"\n- Centered node below middle: \"The specified products form a basis\\nat every lower positive height\\nTheorem 12.5\"\n- Bottom centered node: \"Fracture and rational dimensions\\ngive the ordered filtration\\nProposition 2.1\"\nEdges:\n- Directed downward arrow from \"Finite frames, transfers, and compact supports Sections 3–5\" to \"Coefficient finiteness and full-frame rows Sections 6–8\".\n- A path from the bottom of \"Coefficient finiteness and full-frame rows Sections 6–8\" and a path from the bottom of \"One integral sphere-cochain family Sections 9–10\" meet at a horizontal joining bar, from which a single downward arrow points to \"The coefficient unit generates the specified exterior module Proposition 11.4\".\n- Directed downward arrow from \"The coefficient unit generates the specified exterior module Proposition 11.4\" to \"The specified products form a basis at every lower positive height Theorem 12.5\".\n- Directed downward arrow from \"The specified products form a basis at every lower positive height Theorem 12.5\" to \"Fracture and rational dimensions give the ordered filtration Proposition 2.1\"."
